A great soul such as Sadguru Kabir Sahib would not call his own guru and his followers unwise. This compels one to the conclusion that this line must be an interpolation. Kabir himself says: 'aape guru kriya kichhu keenho, nirgun chalakh lakhaai; sahaj samadhi unmuni jaage, sahaj milai saguraai' (the Guru himself performed some act, revealing a glimpse of the attributeless; through it the natural samadhi awakens in the mind beyond mind, and the true guru's grace is met with ease) — from these words it follows that Kabirji was Ramchandra's supreme devotee and worshipper. Having seen Kabirji's statements refuting the avatars, some commentators, worshippers, and scholars say that Kabirji also carried Muslim cultural influences. But looking at the actual words themselves, these scholars' claims appear false. Since the Bijak is a compiled text, differences of a line or two, and variant readings, are found among its different manuscript copies."

In the Samagam, in the given Shabda (Word) 8, "Saints, whatever comes and goes is maya," it is said that whoever remembers Ram [in that framework] is blind, without understanding — and this controversial statement has been read as showing opposition to devotion to Ram. To counter this, [commentators] argue, using the words found in Shabda 4, Kabirwani Year 1, Issue 11, page 5, that Kabirji was in fact a supporter of devotion to Ram; and accordingly it is stated so also in the Samagam of Vasana and elsewhere; and in the Bijak, under "Aspashta" [the unclear/obscure section], Shabda 5, one finds "see the explanation" — and on this basis it is claimed that Kabirji's assent to devotion to Ram has been established. The words of Shabda 4, beginning "aape guru kripa keenhi" [you, the guru, showed grace], occur as Shabda 7 or in some such order in other Bijak texts — but the line containing these words actually belongs to the Shabda that begins "santo kahi to ko patipai" [O saints, tell me, who then attains the Lord]. In this way, devout people have sought to prove that Kabir accepted devotion to Ram. Kabir did not accept the ten avatars, however — there is another verse [pad] on this too. In Grantha-18, page 118, there is a rameni.

|| Rameni ||

_Niraakaar nirgun nahin paaya, parathamai ekahi aapai aapa. ||1||_
(The formless, attributeless one could not be found — in the very beginning, He alone existed, by Himself.)

_Tab nahin pavan aakaasa, tab nahin chand sooraj parakaaya. ||2||_
(Then there was no wind, no sky; then there was no light of moon or sun, no embodied form.)

_Tab nahin paanch tattva gun teeni, tab nahin maaya srishtaj keeni. ||3||_
(Then there were no five elements, no three gunas; then maya had not fashioned creation.)

_Tab nahin sargun sakal pasaara, tab nahin keene dasau avataara. ||4||_
(Then there was no manifest expanse of qualities at all; then the ten avatars had not been taken.)

_Tab nahin machh kachh aur vaaraaha, tab nahin Narsimha Harnaakansh maara. ||5||_
(Then there was no fish, no tortoise, no boar; then Hiranyakashipu had not been slain as Narsimha.)

_Tab nahin Krishna Kans Bal Baavan, tab nahin Raghupati tab nahin Raavan. ||6||_
(Then there was no Krishna, no Kansa, no Bali, no Vaman; then there was no Raghupati [Ram], and no Ravan.)

_Tab nahin shruti Ved Puraan, tab nahin Kaazi Kiteb Kuraana. ||7||_
(Then there were no Shrutis, no Vedas, no Puranas; then there was no Qazi, no scripture, no Quran.)

_Tab nahin saayet saat taranga, tab nahin Sarasvati Jamuna Ganga. ||8||_
(Then there were no waves upon the seven seas; then there was no Sarasvati, Yamuna, or Ganga.)

_Tab nahin paap dharam guru shishya, tab nahin pathan gunanka lekh. ||9||_
(Then there was no sin or virtue, no guru or disciple; then there was no reading, counting, or writing.)

_Tab nahin jog jagan vrat pooja, tab nahin devi daiv nahin dooja. ||10||_
(Then there was no yoga, yajna, vow, or worship; then there was no goddess, no deity, nothing else.)

|| Sakhi ||

_Kahe Kabir vichaareekai, tab ek kartap naahin.
Param purush aapai hutai, agam agochar maanhi._
(Kabir says, having reflected: at that time not even a single act was being done. The Supreme Being alone existed by Himself, within the unapproachable, imperceptible reality.)

_Agam agochar gam nahin, jahaan jhilmil jot.
Tahaan Kabira bandagi, paata punna nahi chhot._
(Where that unapproachable, imperceptible one cannot be reached, where there is only a shimmering radiance — there, says Kabira, is true worship; there, no gain of merit and no touch of sin remain.)

Das Kabirji says: when in the world there was not yet anything like the Brahm-tattva that transcends the three gunas, at that very first moment only You, the Parabrahm Parmatma, existed. Then there was no wind or sky; then there was no light of moon or sun; then there were no five elements and three gunas; then there was neither creation nor maya. Then nothing pervaded everywhere in manifest, embodied form; then the ten avatars had not been taken. Then Ram was not fish, tortoise, or boar; then Hiranyakashipu had not been slain in the form of Narsimha; then Krishna had not slain Kansa. Then there was no Ram, no Ravan. Then there were no Shrutis, Vedas, Puranas. Then there was no Qazi, no scripture, no Quran; then there were no waves upon the seven oceans. Then there was no triveni confluence of Sarasvati, Yamuna, and Ganga. Then there was no sin or virtue, no guru or disciple; then there was no reckoning of learning and counting. Then there was no yoga, yajna, vow, or worship; then there was no god, goddess, or anything else.

The Broken Raas — The Raas Faltered

While discussing exclusive devotion (ananya bhakti), it is said that Gopaldas dispelled the confusion about whether the Supreme Being's form is with-form (sakar) or formless (nirakar) by declaring that the Lord's true nature is beyond the form-endowed divine essence in which He manifests through the ten avatars — and thereby the chapter has been opened on the Complete Parabrahm Parmatma whom we are to worship. That supreme reality which is the meeting-point of the named-and-formed and the nameless-formless, of sagun and nirgun — the flute-charmer Morli Manohar — is like the water held in Radha's hands; the waves that arise in that water are the avatars. Just as those waves break and dissolve, so the avatars come to an end. But it is the essence of the flute-charmer Himself — the unmoving Parabrahm, Shri Krishna-Ram, who is beyond all avatars — whom it has been resolved to worship. For the sake of His devotees the Lord comes. [Now] the raas faltered, and something went amiss.

It came to a halt; a break occurred.

_Bhagat manorath Jivana, main dhar kroti avataar.
Ek daski kaha chali, jo bhagat mohe praan aadhaar._
(For the sake of My devotees' heartfelt wishes, O Jivana, I would take on a crore of avatars. What then is the mere talk of ten? — for My devotees are the very support of My life-breath.)

Maharaj Jivandasji says: the Lord says, "For the sake of My devotees' wishes and desires I am ready to take avatar a crore times over — so what wonder is there in speaking of only ten avatars? For My devotees are exceedingly dear to Me."

The Lord's raas-lila is unbroken (akhand) — it does not cease even for as long as it takes to close and open one's eyes; that is, this divine play is never interrupted. In support of this, the words of Hit Harivanshji are given.

_Saamaane saam jhulaavat jhoole Jamunaaki teer,
sadaa vasant hot Vrindaavan rachyo Hit Harivansh bal bheerye._
(Facing one another, they swing upon the swing on the bank of the Yamuna; it is ever springtime in Vrindavan — so has Hit Harivansh, filled with fervor, described it.)

Hit Harivansh says: on the banks of the Yamuna, upon a swing, Lord Krishna swings Radhaji. Thus in Vrindavan there is always joy and delight as of a spring festival; the raas enacted there fills Hit Harivansh with delight. Since the raas is unbroken, there is no need to think, on the notion of the ten avatars, that the Lord manifests in various forms and then dissolves away. Rather, the Lord takes avatar for the sake of His devotees. About what happened when the Lord's raas was broken, Kabirji says:

_Kabir Ved bada na vedasi, nahin Gokulki vrajanaar.
Unhe sahaj na paai, rahi pokaar pokaar. ||1||_
(Kabir says: the Veda is not great enough for this truth, nor are the Braj-women of Gokul great enough — they could not attain that natural union with ease, and were left crying out in lament.)

Das Kabirji says: to attain the essence and mystery of the Lord's love, the Veda itself, however great, is not sufficient; nor can even those who know the Veda attain, or help others attain, this supreme reality. Nor is the stature of the Braj-women of Gokul so great, for they could not easily and simply attain the full bliss of that love; so when the circle of the raas broke, they became distressed and agitated, crying out to the Lord in the pain of separation.

_Prem na peeno Gopika, kachhuk shank rahi man maanhi.
Sur muni dekhan lage Jivana, varti taaki chhaanhi. ||2||_
(The gopis did not fully drink of that love — a trace of doubt remained in their minds. O Jivana, when the gods and sages began to watch, its shadow-influence fell upon them.)

Maharaj Jivandasji says: the gopis could not fully attain the joy of love in the raas-lila, because a slight trace of pride still lingered within them — for the gods and sages watched their sport, and the influence of being so watched fell upon their minds, and so the raas was broken.

Vrindavan's swans, chakoras, chatakas, cuckoos, trees, creepers, vines, the multitude of flowers, the cows, calves, cowherds, gopis, and the playful sport of the gracious Lord — all of this is unbroken (akhand). At the end of the cosmic cycle, the five elements, the three gunas, and the fourteen worlds are dissolved, but Vrindavan remains unbroken. Even at the end of the cycle, not a single leaf falls from the flute-bearer's tree of this forest. Only where time and maya have influence does dissolution occur. But in Vrindavan there is the Lord's own maya, His own tenderness — the tenderness of love, the tenderness of love. The raas was broken, yet Kabirji offers this counsel to the gopis:

_Kabir sahaj ma chhaandes sundari, tumhe sahajanandaki aan.
Tan jaataan jo pan rahai, to nirbhe gade nishaan._
(Kabir says: O beautiful ones, do not abandon your natural state; you are bound by the vow of natural bliss. Even if the body should perish, if your resolve remains, then you shall plant your victory-banner fearlessly.)

Das Kabirji says: O beautiful gopis! Do not abandon your natural state (sahajavastha); do not abandon your undistorted state. You have been enjoined to hold to the undistorted state of Prem-Lakshana Bhakti [love-natured devotion] to the Lord. So even if your body should perish, if your resolve is preserved, do not concern yourselves with the body; by doing so you shall fearlessly sound the drum of your victory.

_Kabir trigun rahit Kahaanuo, jine rachyo akhandit raas.
Prem jot Braj sundari, tahaan baare maas vilaas._
(Kabir says: this Krishna, free of the three gunas, has fashioned the unbroken raas; the beauties of Braj are like flames of love — there, delight goes on through all twelve months of the year.)

Das Kabirji says: this Lord Krishna is beyond the three gunas — He who has fashioned this unbroken raas. The beauties of Braj are like the flame of Prem-Lakshana Bhakti; and so in Vrindavan, joy and delight continue unbroken through all twelve months.

Through lines from a kirtan of Maharaj Adhyaruji, this raas has been described:

_Mor peench Chandra mugar sir sohe, nij maaya dev tribhovan sohe.
Sohe gunjaakal haaro, Hari Hari._
(The peacock-feather crest with its moon-mark adorns His head; through His own maya, the Lord adorns all three worlds. The garland of gunja-berries adorns Him — Hari, Hari!)

In Lord Krishna's crown, the moon-shaped crest of peacock feathers shines; such is the Lord who, through His own maya, shines throughout all three worlds. Around His neck shines a garland of gunja-berries.

In this way, while the Lord was playing the raas, the gods and sages came rushing to watch, and began hailing Him with cries of victory, showering flowers upon Him. They said:

_Dhan dhan Gokulani Brijnaare, kun punya keedhalaan re.
Dhan dhan Gokulani Brijnaar._
(Blessed, blessed are the Braj-women of Gokul — what merit must they have earned! Blessed, blessed are the Braj-women of Gokul.)

"Blessed, blessed are the women of Gokul — what merit they must have earned, that they get to play such a raas! Blessed, blessed are these women of Gokul" — the gods praised them thus, and because of this praise a feeling of self-importance, of being especially fortunate, arose in the gopis' minds. But this feeling did not arise in Radhaji, and so the Lord went into hiding (antardhyan) together with Radhaji. Jivandasji said: "Brothers, true love was pointlessly interrupted, so that it became as if it had never happened, because of separation from the Lord." If even a shadow of wickedness touches it, then even true love becomes false; therefore one should set aside distortion and love the Lord without any desire for reward. Again, he gave a second sakhi:

_Prem na peeno Gopika, kachhuk shank rahi man maanhi.
Sur muni dekhan lage Jivana, varti taaki chhaanhi. ||1||_
(The gopis did not fully drink of that love — a trace of doubt remained in their minds. O Jivana, when the gods and sages began to watch, its shadow-influence fell upon them.)

The shadow of beings such as the gods and sages is called the shadow of the wicked, because the gods are given to pleasure and the sages are worshippers of the gods, so both are counted alike in this. The meaning of the "shadow of the wicked" is this: if one holds supreme, exclusive devotion (para-bhakti, ananya-bhakti) toward Krishna, then one's attention should not turn toward gods or worldly people. Radhaji had such love for the Lord that He took her along with Him as He disappeared, but even she was touched by this influence of wickedness — the feeling arose in her, "I am supremely fortunate, since the Lord keeps me with Him and has become invisible" — and so, while He was carrying Radhaji along, the Lord said, "if you cling to the branch of a tree, I will change My shoulder"; and having said this, He left her hanging from the branch of a tree and Himself vanished. Thus Radhaji's plight became even worse than that of the other gopis. All the gopis gathered together, and, filled with regret, said, "the raas was pointlessly interrupted." Thus even a subtle trace of ego creates a disturbance in devotion.

_Khoji aap saraahataan, teen baatki dhaat.
Budh ochhi vaachaa akal, aavaradaa ghat jaat._
(Khoji says: in praising oneself, three things suffer harm — one's intellect diminishes, one's speech becomes foolish, and one's lifespan grows shorter.)

Maharaj Khojiji says: from self-praise — praising oneself — we suffer harm in three respects: our intellect diminishes, our speech becomes a laughingstock, and our lifespan is shortened.

_Sumirat jinke charanko, moh jaat hai bhaag.
Nirmohi vah hoy to, kaa acharajki baat._
(By remembering whose feet, delusion flees away — if He Himself is free of delusion, what wonder is there in that?)

_Mohi Dashrath Laal hai, nirmohi Nandlaal.
Ve ban ban dhoondhat phire, inhi taaji Braj baal._
(Dashrath's son [Ram] was bound by delusion; Nandlal [Krishna] is free of delusion. He wandered from forest to forest searching, while He at once left behind the young women of Braj.)

By remembering whose feet our delusion departs — if such a Lord is Himself free of delusion and desire, what wonder is there in that? Ram, the son of Dashrath, was bound by delusion; Krishna was free of delusion. Ram wandered through forest after forest searching for Sita, whereas Shri Krishna simply left the gopis of Braj behind.

|| The Unbroken Raas: The Natural Certainty of the Lover — Master of the Court and Master of the Chamber ||
|| The Unbroken Raas: The Highest Culmination of Love-Devotion ||
|| The Unbroken Raas: The Natural Certainty of the Lover — Master of the Court and Master of the Chamber ||

_Prem bhakti ekai palak, kohi varasko yog.
Prem bhakti sab yog hai, yog prem bivan rog._
(One single moment of love-devotion is worth more than the yoga of countless years. Love-devotion is itself the complete yoga, while yoga without love is merely a disease.)

Even if love-natured devotion (prem-lakshana bhakti) lasts for only a single moment, it is greater than crores of years of yogic practice. Love-devotion is in itself the complete yoga, whereas yoga practiced without love, practiced only for show, is like a disease that neither kills nor lets one grow — it is merely painful, like an affliction.

To support the view that the raas is regarded as unbroken, a pad of Narsinh Mehta is given.

|| Raag Kedaro ||

_Shaamloji sukhanu nidhaan re sajani.
Ven vaahine vahaale tedi ramaadyaan, dei karkalade maan re sajani. ||tek|| ||1||
Raam ramataan sukhad mohyaa, muniji bhoolyaa dhyaan re sajani.
Paamyaa mahaaras amo raakhi nav jaanyo, kaain ek keedhun maan re sajani. ||2||
Mananu kaaran Mohan jaane, Hari thayaa antardhyaan re sajani.
Beh vachan bole re Vraj vanitaa, kaahu nav deethaa Kahaan re sajani. ||3||
Vyaaku thai re Vrindaavan shodhyaa,
Aatur thai antargat joyun, madhyathi pragatyaa Kahaan re sajani.
Narsaiyaachaa swaami bhale malyaa, paamyaa param nidhaan re sajani. ||4||_
(O friend, Shyamji is a treasure-house of bliss. Playing His flute, the Beloved called us and made us dance the raas, honoring us by holding our hands, O friend. Playing with Him we were enchanted by that bliss, and even the sages forgot their meditation. We attained the supreme essence of love, but did not recognize You for who You were, O friend, and let a little pride arise. Mohan knew what was in our minds, and Hari became hidden. The women of Braj spoke words of anguish, saying, 'We can nowhere see Kahan.' Distressed, we searched all through Vrindavan; eager, we looked within, and from our very midst Kahan appeared. Narsaiya's Lord has been graciously met — we have attained the supreme treasure.)

O friend, Lord Krishna is the treasure-house that bestows supreme bliss. O friend, the beloved Lord played His flute and called us, welcoming and honoring us with a gentle smile, and made us play the raas — and even the sages forgot to meditate. O friend, we attained the supreme essence of love, but we could not fully understand You, and some pride arose within us. O friend, Lord Krishna came to know of the pride that lay in our minds, and so the Lord became hidden. O friend, and so the gopis of Braj, overwhelmed by separation, began to utter words of lament. Becoming distraught, they searched throughout Vrindavan but could nowhere see the Lord. O friend, then, restless and anguished, they looked within themselves, and there they found the Lord, like a treasure of supreme love and bliss.

In this chapter on the Unbroken [Raas], the highest culmination of love-devotion has been shown. The unbrokenness of the raas has been examined. It has been raised for consideration: the Lord manifested from the midst of the gopis — how and why did He manifest, and where did He become hidden? Everyone says the raas faltered, that a flaw came upon it, an obstruction arose, it went wrong, a delay occurred — so then how did the raas come to be called unbroken? This confusion has been resolved, and to show that the raas is indeed unbroken and never truly breaks, Narsinh Mehta's pad in the Sindhuda raga has been given.

|| Ram Sindhuko ||

_Jeere dhanya tun dhanya tun em kahai Shri Hari, Narsinho maaro bhakt saacho.
Mooki purushaatan sakhi re veshe thayo, taahraa premthi hun re naachyo. ||1||
Jeere mujmaan tujmaan bhed nahin naagaraa, maan maari tun ved vaani.
Haju tujne prateet na upaje, mokalyun mein tune taadhu paani. ||2||
Jeere mosaalun karyun kaan-e visar, tujne haar aapyo pratyaksh bhoop.
Chaud lokmaan maare duj samo ko nahin, taaheru maaher ek roop. ||3||
Jeere tohro akshar saambhale gaaye, tehnaa kul sahit paavan thaaye.
Bhaage Narsinh-o meethaan boli shun reejhavo, taare kar jodi Krishnaji sam khaaye. ||4||_
('Oh, blessed are you, blessed are you,' says Shri Hari: 'Narsinh is My true devotee. Setting aside your manhood, you took the form and disposition of a sakhi; out of love for you, I too danced.' 'There is no difference between you and Me, O clever one; take My word as truly as scripture. If you still have no faith in this, know that I sent you the cold water Myself.' 'Why do you forget the gift-ceremony I performed for you — I Myself, in visible form as king, gave you the garland. In all fourteen worlds there is no one else like you to Me; your honor is unique.' 'Whoever hears and sings your composition becomes purified, together with his whole family.' Narsinh says: 'Why do You please me with such sweet words?' — and then, folding his hands, Krishnaji swore that it was so.)

'Well done!' says the Lord, 'blessed are you, blessed are you, O Narsinh! You are My true devotee. You set aside your manhood and took on the disposition of a sakhi, and out of love for you I acted just as you said. O clever one, there is no difference between Me and you — believe that this true, well-founded statement of Mine is correct. Do you still not feel assured? It was I Myself who sent you the cold water. It was I Myself who performed your gift-ceremony and gave you the garland in the very presence of King Ramandalik. In all fourteen worlds there is no one else like you to Me. My form and your form are one and the same. Whoever sings and hears your bhajans and kirtans becomes purified, together with his whole family.' Narsinh Mehta says, 'O Lord, why do You please me with such sweet, sweet words?' — at that, the Lord, agreeing wholeheartedly, folded his hands and, with an oath, said, 'Truly, I regard you as My true devotee.'

In Patra Bhagwan Bapu, Grantha No. 1, page 60, Pad 130, of the Haarmala, there is a pad of similar sentiment.

|| Kadarja Sindhuko ||

_Jeere dhanya tun dhanya tun em kahe Shri Hari, trigun rahit mohyun man maaru.
Trigun rahit man thayun taaru.
Jeere kot brahmaandpati karahun vinati, pooran mune hridayaamaan dhyaan taaru. ||tek||
Narsaiya tun vachan maan maaru.
Jeere Brahma Shankar Sati (Shruti) Sanakaadik aade jati, Shesh Mahesh (Shuk) ghare dhyaan maaru.
Man karm vachne vare mugatne anusare, evi mugati taare charane vaaru. ||1||
Maare jevi Vraj sundari tevo j Narsaiyo, ene niramal mane maaro jas gaayo.
Rank hun ank bhari urpar raakhio, jem kusumni paankhadi heet saahyo. ||2||
Jeere kunj leelaae tun madhukar maahvaa, purush naame koi paas aave.
Aade tahaan Shri Hari Brij vanitaa khari, tahaan Narsaiyo charanni rog naahe. ||3||
Narsaiya vinaa mune kon ladaave._
('Blessed are you, blessed are you,' says Shri Hari, 'even though I am beyond the three gunas, My mind has been drawn to you; your mind too has become free of the three gunas. I, the Lord of countless universes, entreat you: My complete meditation is fixed within your heart. Narsinh, accept these words of Mine as true. Brahma, Shankar, the Shrutis, Sanaka and the other primal ascetics, Shesh, Mahesh, and Shukdev all keep their meditation fixed on Me. Whatever liberation people seek through mind, deed, and word — that liberation I offer freely at your feet.' 'Just as dear to Me as the beauties of Braj is Narsinh himself, who with a pure mind has sung My praise. Though I am humble, I have been held close to your bosom, as a flower holds its petals close.' 'In the playful groves you are like a honey-drinking bee; only one who has cast off manhood can come near. There truly reside the wives of Braj, devoted to Shri Hari; there, at Narsinh's feet, no ailment of separation remains. Without Narsinh, who else would so lovingly indulge Me?')

'Ah,' says the Lord, 'well done to you, for even though I am beyond the three gunas, My mind has been drawn to you. Your mind too has come to transcend the three gunas. Ah yes, I, the master of countless universes, entreat you: My full attention rests within My heart upon you. O Narsinh, know that what I say here is exactly true. Ah yes, Brahma, Shankar, Parvati, the Shrutis, and Sanaka and the other ancient ascetics and renunciants, as well as beings such as Sheshnag, Mahadev, and Shukdev, keep their contemplation fixed on Me. The liberation that people and ascetics seek to attain through meditation, knowledge, and the performance of rites, with mind, word, and deed — that very liberation I place under your command. To Me, you, Narsinh, are just like the gopis of Braj who perform love-devotion to Me; you are their equal, for you have performed My devotion with a pure, unblemished mind. Just as the petals of a flower are held tightly clasped together, so too I am, as it were, helplessly held, for you have held Me in your lap. Ah yes — in the play of the groves you delighted, reveling in pleasure like a bee, for in that play no one possessing the disposition of manhood can approach. From the very first, the true gopis of the Lord of Braj are there, and in that very state Narsinh too takes delight in the dust of their feet. In this play of Braj, who but Narsinh could please Me with love-devotion and lovingly indulge Me?'

Manhood is not found only in men — it is found in women as well. If a woman exerts her power and takes pride on the strength of her beauty, charm, skill, or status, that is "manhood" in a woman. In the same way, if a man sets aside his own ego and, through love and devotion, accepts refuge in the Lord, then that man is regarded as having "womanhood." Thus, whoever is free of ego is reckoned to have this womanhood. One who remains in the natural state (sahajavastha), that is, in the undistorted disposition, comes to attain love-devotion. Here, one who practices devotion while holding on to self-interest — on such a person the Lord bestows grace only to the extent of that self-interest. To show this sentiment, a morning kirtan (prabhatiyu) is presented, showing what the natural state (sahaj) of the gopis is, and what it teaches.

|| Prabhati || Kadakha Kedaro ||

_Te naarathi shun sukhiaa thaayes Shaamalaa, je naari naath kahi vinay karase.
Aafli aafli aavase aasare, jo rasiyaa tanu barad dharase. ||1||
Tehna dhiraj gun chaaturi aahaj lehese, ehavaa maanani maramnaa vachan varase.
Nirgun ati Shaamalo subah te me lahyo, nirakhavaa Krishnane nayan tarase. ||2||
Jeere meetra maahaaro sadaae prabhu avaraan tanu, muj vinaa e ras kon bharase.
Narsaiyaacho swaami jagat thamase sadaa, pan rooparas magan sang aanhaan j tharase._
(O Shyam, how could You find happiness through a woman who merely calls You her Lord and makes polite requests to You? Each such woman comes only for her own selfish refuge, even while claiming the vow of a true lover. She keeps only His patience and cleverness for her own purposes; such a proud woman's words fall full of hidden barbs. 'I have attained the utterly attributeless Shyam this very morning,' she boasts, while her eyes only long to gaze upon Krishna. Oh, my companion is always the Lord of others too — without me, who else could fill this love with such fullness? Narsaiya's Lord always keeps still amid the world, but engrossed in the joy of my form, He remains fixed right here.)

'O Krishna, how then will You find the joy of love-devotion through a self-interested, desire-laden gopi-woman? How will You expect the happiness of love, when such a woman, who humbly prays to You saying "my Lord, my Master," will suddenly, stumbling and falling, come to take Your refuge, presenting herself as one holding firm devotion to love for You? In this way, through the cleverness of her nature — her supposed patience being of little real worth — she will sigh and lament, and such a proud, honor-seeking woman will use words that strike at tender places. My eyes are eager to behold Lord Krishna. Ah yes — this Krishna is My eternal, deeply loving companion, bound to Me by an unbreakable tie; to everyone else He is the Supreme Lord and Master, and so, apart from Me, He may wander throughout the world — but His very body, absorbed in the joy of love-devotion, will settle and remain fixed right here, in Me.'

Only where the shock of the ego called manhood does not occur can the water of love-devotion remain stable. Thus Narsinh Mehta, having set aside manhood and taken on the surrendered devotion of sakhi-bhava (the companion's disposition), became worthy of beholding the Lord's raas. Such a state of being free from distortion is called the natural state (sahaj avastha). The Lord manifested from the midst of the gopis — that is, when the dualistic states such as honor and dishonor, pride and shame, joy and sorrow, come to an end, that is called "the midst" (madhya); and it was when the gopis reached this natural state that the Lord manifested from their midst. As for why He became hidden (antardhyan) — when a disturbance occurs in the state of love-devotion, love dissolves into waves and vanishes; that is called antardhyan. There the raas faltered, but Ram [the Lord] is unbroken, because the Lord's love-devotion never once ceases. When the endeavor of the paths of knowledge, action, and yoga meets with a shock, then all these — japa, tapa, and the like, the thieving "merchants" of ritual and duty — create obstruction in love-devotion. But such natural love-devotion, the gopi-natured devotion, comes about through the adoption of womanhood; yet giving up manhood is very difficult indeed.

Revered Yadunath Maharaj writes, in Lintiyu-57, page 6 (verso):

"The prabhatiyu that begins 'Dhanya tun dhanya tun,' spoken by Shri Hari, is of great importance. Bringing womanhood into a man's body is no small matter. When Mirabai went to meet Jiv Gosai, Jiv Gosai said, 'I do not look upon the face of a woman.' At this Mirabai said, 'What — is there still a man in Vrindavan?'"

Revered Yadunath, in Lintiyu No. 1, page 6, writes:

"The prabhatiyu that begins 'Dhanya tun dhanya tun,' spoken by Shri Hari, is of great importance. Bringing womanhood into a man's body is no small matter. When Mirabai went to meet Jiv Gosai, Jiv Gosai said, 'I do not look upon the face of a woman.' At this Mirabai said, 'What — is there still a man in Vrindavan?'"

Revered Yadunath, in Lintiyu No. 1, page 6, writes: "I was going to give some needed items to the students of the household in Vadodara. I was sitting on a bench on the platform at Miyagam, when a Muslim person came by, dressed in women's clothing; so, on some pretext, I struck up a conversation with him. From this I learned that in this whole path, throughout all of Hindustan, we are only three or four persons, and he lives in the guise of a sakhi."

Bhagwandas, the writer of the commentary on the Bhaktamal, lived in sakhi-form; his sakhi-name was Roopkala. He passed away a few years ago; he had been a school inspector at Mokri.

Just as Revered Yadunath saw a man dressed as a woman, I too once, on a bus, saw a man dressed in women's attire; he even had earrings in his ears. At that time I recalled the incident of Revered Yadunath, but I did not speak with him. In essence, there is a difference between merely going about with an outward appearance and living with the inward disposition. One may have a wish for womanhood, but that should not be about the difference of sex — rather, this "womanhood" should be for the sake of the disposition of non-attachment. After discussing the natural state (sahaj) of the gopis, it now turns to discuss Kabirji's natural state, saying:

_Kabir na kachhu kiya na kar shaka, na karane jog shareer.
Jo kachhu kiya so Hari kiya, taathe bhaya Kabir Kabir._
(Kabir says: I have done nothing, nor could I do anything, nor is this body fit to do anything. Whatever has been done, Hari alone has done it — and because of that, Kabir has come to be called Kabir.)

Das Kabir says: neither in the past have I been able to do anything, nor am I able to now, and neither is this body fit to do anything in the future. Whatever has been done at all, all of it the Lord Himself has done and caused to be done — and so it is Your own power alone that dwells within me.

_Kaayen vaachaa manasendriyair vaa buddhyaatmanaa vaa prakriteh svabhaavaat,
karomi yat tat sakalam parasmai Naaraayanaayeti samarthayaami._
(Whatever I do — with body, speech, mind and senses, intellect or self, or by the very nature of my constitution — all of it I dedicate wholly to the Supreme Narayana.)

'O Lord! Whatever I do at all times — with body and senses, with mind and intellect, or by my very nature — all of it has been offered and dedicated to You alone, for it is Yours.'

_Dehendriyothi man-buddhithi vaa svabhaavthi je karto sadaa hun,
Te sarva arpu tamane j devaah badhun tamaaru tamane samarpu.
Sattaa tamaari mujmaan vase chhe, tamo thaki hun karto janaank,
Karun, badhun hun tam-naath-kaaje, kashun na maaru, sadhalu tamaaru.
Badhun tamaaru, tamane samarpun, sveekaarasho naath! tamo tamaaru.
Swaami tamo, sevak hun tamaaro, shreepaadmaan vaas mane samarpo.
Swaami yathaa sevakni kanethi, prasann thaaye nijvastu paami,
Tevi j reete mujne dayaalo, jayaa tani drishti thaki nihaalo._
(Whatever I do, always, with body and senses, with mind and intellect, or by nature — all of it, O God, I offer to You; everything, whatever is Yours, I dedicate to You. Your power dwells within me; it is by You that I am made to act; whatever I do, I do it all for Your sake, O Lord; nothing is mine, all is Yours. Everything is Yours; I offer it to You — accept, O Lord, what is already Yours. You are the Master, I am Your servant; grant me a place at Your holy feet. Just as a master, receiving back his own possession from his servant, becomes pleased, so too, O Compassionate One, look upon me with that same gracious, victorious glance.)

_Jo kuchh kiya so Hari kiya, main kachhu kiya naahi.
Jo kahun kahi ki main kiya, tum hi the mujh maanhi._
(Whatever was done, Hari alone did it — I have done nothing at all. If I should ever say that I did something, it was You alone who dwelt within me.)

Das Kabir says: O Lord! All of it, everything, You Yourself have done. Even if I should say I have done something, it was You alone who were present within me as the capable power behind it.

_Meraa mujmen kachhun nahi, jo hai so teraa.
Teraa tujku sopte, kahaa lagegaa meraa._
(Nothing that is 'mine' truly exists in me; whatever there is, is Yours. In returning what is Yours to You, what of 'mine' shall be lost?)

_Kahaa lagegaa meraa, tamaarun tamaari paase.
(Trustee) saagreet sam chhun huy, aaptaan maaru shu jase.
Trikam saphal kar pheraa, paramaarath jhadapi sahi.
Jo hai so teraa, meraa mujmen kachhun nahin._
(What shall I lose? — what is Yours goes back to You. I am but like a custodian; what will I lose by giving it back? O Trikam, make this round of human birth fruitful, and swiftly grasp hold of the true purpose. Whatever exists is Yours; nothing that is 'mine' truly exists in me.)

Nothing at all has been accomplished by me, through myself; whatever strength, intellect, and so on I have is Yours alone. So then, what of mine will be lost in handing over what is Yours to You? What will I lose by giving back what is Yours? I am merely like a caretaker of Your possessions — what is lost by returning them? Trikamdas says: make this round of human birth of yours fruitful, and take hold of good deeds without delay. Whatever exists is Yours alone; there is nothing of mine in it.

Kabirji has shown the sentiment of the natural, detached disposition (sahaj tatasthapanu).

_Kabir sahaj sahaj sabkoy kahe, par sahaj na cheenhe koi.
Paancho raakhe parasten, sahaj kahaavai soi. ||1||_
(Kabir says: everyone speaks of 'sahaj, sahaj' [the natural state], but no one truly recognizes what sahaj is. He who keeps the five senses from touching their objects — he alone is truly called sahaj.)

Das Kabir says: everyone keeps talking about "sahaj, sahaj" [the undistorted state], but no one truly understands what should be called this natural non-attachment. One who restrains the five senses that go out toward sense-objects — that alone is called the natural state (sahajavastha), the state of detachment.

_Kabir sahaj sahaj sabkoy kahe, par sahaj na cheenhe koi.
Jo sahjai milai, sahaj kahaavai soi. ||2||_
(Kabir says: everyone speaks of 'sahaj, sahaj,' but no one truly recognizes what sahaj is. That which is attained naturally, with ease — that alone is truly called sahaj.)

Das Kabirji says: everyone keeps talking about sahaj, sahaj, but no one can say whether this "sahaj" is truly sahaj or not. Only that disposition of naturalness by adopting which one attains the Lord can be called the true natural disposition. Good disposition, good thought, and the like are what is called sahaj.

_Main dadhi mahi saate Jivana, paayo Padupati raay.
Shareer sonpu aapno, to leelaa kaise thaay. ||3||_
(In exchange for curd and buttermilk, O Jivana, I attained Padupati, the King. But if I surrender this body of mine entirely, then how could His playful sport ever take place?)

Maharaj Jivandasji says: in exchange for my craving to make use of curd and buttermilk-butter, I have taken the avatar of Yadupati Shri Krishna in order to obtain that buttermilk and butter. If I were to accept my own existence as non-different, in absolute oneness with the gopas and gopis — that is, if my body held complete unity with the gopas and gopis — then how could the delightful play of curd and butter ever take place?

Having spoken of the gopis' natural Prem-Lakshana Bhakti, now, in speaking of the natural Prem-Lakshana Bhakti of Kabirji and Narsinh Mehta, it is said that the Lord experiences love-devotion in two ways. An example of a king is given. A king enjoys the delight of love with his queens in the inner chambers of his palace, and also conducts the administration of the affairs and revenue of the kingdom in his court. In these two states, the delight of love is of a different kind in each. The king conducts the affairs of the court with the help of his minister, and it is the king who receives the results of this. But when the king has retired to rest within the inner chambers of his palace with his queens, there is no need there for a minister — there, the enjoyment of pleasure and delight can be given by none but the queens. When matters of the court arise, the king himself must leave the pleasure of the inner chambers to attend to them. And if there were no queens in the palace, then the affairs of those who come and go there could not be looked after by anyone else. Thus, for the king, there is no real difference between the pleasure enjoyed in these two places, the inner chambers and the court — both kinds of pleasure are just the same. The officer who administers the king's court, who tends the court of love-devotion, is Namdev-Kabirji; and the Master who enjoys love-devotion within the palace's inner chambers is the Lord Kripanath. And it is Narsinh Mehta who, within such a palace, is the giver of supreme pleasure. The natural Prem-Lakshana Bhakti of both Namdev-Kabir and Narsinh Mehta is one and the same. Narsinh Mehta is the one who tends to the Lord's love within the inner chambers. That is to say, Namdev-Kabir and Narsinh Mehta are both forms belonging to the Lord Himself; the two are not different — they are one and the same. The minister was said to be the one who tends to the affairs of the court, with no role in the bedchamber; whereas Narsinh Mehta is said to be the giver of delight in the bedchamber — yet the natural state of both is one. Looking at the Bhairav pad, relating to this bedchamber, which Kabir himself sang, it is shown that Kabir and Narsinh hold one and the same standing.

|| Bhairav ||

_Mai pahuaa vimal jash gadhzaa, charankamal Raajaa Raamji ke gaayaa.
Bhanat naat jet kachhu anamai, nai sadkaa le aavaa. ||tek||
Bheetar mahel podhe Kamalaapati, tahaan jaai main gaavaa.
Taathe prabhu meraa chamki jaagile, ko daas bandagi aavaa. ||1||_
(I have attained pure, radiant glory; I have sung of the lotus feet of King Ramji. Whatever I sing, [unclear], I have brought as a true offering. Within the palace, the Lotus-Lord (Kamalapati) lay resting; going there, I sang. At that, my Lord awoke with a start — [asking] which devotee has come in such devotion?)

_Kari sanmaan aasan mohe deeno. Kaahaa daan tohe deeje. Swaarathke hum naahi lobhiye. Bhakti daan mohe deeje. ||2||_ (He honored me and gave me a seat, asking what gift He should give me. I said I am not greedy for selfish gain — give me the gift of devotion.)

_Pakri baanhe bheetar mohi leena. Sab asthaan deekhlaavaa. Naam nighant tilak aur maalaa. Daas Kabir pehnaavaa. ||3||_ (He caught my arm and drew me inside, and showed me every place; and from the whole treasury of His names He adorned this servant Kabir with His name, with tilak, and with a garland.)

Daas Kabirji says: I, a guest of the Lord, sang His pure, glorious hymns and kirtans in praise of His fame, and sang the glory of the lotus feet of Ram. To a devotee the Lord surely grants fearlessness — He came bearing the gift of surrender and dedication for His devotee. The Lord was resting in His palace; this servant-devotee went there and sang the Lord's praises. Hearing this, the Lord woke with a start and understood that some devotee-servant had come to Him with an earnest plea. The Lord honored me, welcomed me, gave me a seat, and asked what boon He should give me. I said I was not greedy for selfish gain; grant me instead the boon of devotion to You. The Lord took hold of my hand and called me inside, and from all the words in His treasury of names He adorned this devotee Kabir with His own name, with tilak (of gopichandan), and with a garland of tulsi beads.

Thus Kabirji too reached all the way to the Lord's palace, and so he says—

_Kabir dahlikee to sab koi kahai. Mahalkee na kahai koy. Mahalkee to tab kahai. Jo mahalkaa mahrami hoy._ (Kabir says: everyone can speak of the entrance-hall, but none can speak of the palace itself. Only one who is intimate with the palace, familiar with its inner secret, can speak of the palace.)

Daas Kabirji says that everyone can talk about the threshold at the entrance of a royal palace, but no one can describe the beauty of its interior. That inner splendor of the palace can be told only by someone who is an intimate insider, familiar with its private secret.

The dahli (entrance-hall) is the Lord's outer court, the illusion (maya) of creation, while the mahal (palace) is the Supreme Being's highest abode. The dahli is ritual, desire-bound worship; the mahal is the inner soul's desireless, loving devotion.

_Naadi vaadi bahu milai. Karat kaleje chhed. (Koi) takht talekaa naa milaa. Jaason poochhoon bhed._ (One meets many who merely chant or merely argue, wounding the heart with disputation; but none is found who sits beneath the throne, of whom I might ask the secret.)

Daas Kabirji says: those who merely worship the unstruck sound, and mere talkers — scholars of the Vedas, well-versed in the scriptures, given to disputation — one meets many such people, then and now, who are the sort that wound the heart and cut into it. But no one is found who reveals the secret of the highest truth of loving devotion, of whom one could ask the secret of peace and supreme bliss.

_Takht talekaa so kahai. Jo takht talekaa hoy. Maanjh mahalkee ko kahai. Padadaa gaadhaa soy._ (He alone can speak of what lies beneath the throne who himself is beneath the throne; and who can speak of the very heart of the palace, so thick is the veil there.)

Daas Kabirji says only one who is the Lord's own servant, devotee, and attendant can speak of the vision of the Supreme Being — but to enter, to penetrate into the palace (the inner being) of the Imperishable One is rare; no ordinary person can gain entry there, for the knot of maya's veil surrounds it.

_Maanjh mahalkee guru kahai. Dekhaa sab nij gharbaar. Poonji deenhee hoth kar. Padadaa diyaa dathaay._ (Only the guru can speak of the very heart of the palace, for he has seen all of his own house; he has placed the treasure in hand and torn away the veil.)

Daas Kabirji says only the Guru can speak of the highest abode, for he has seen and experienced the Lord's court — the house of loving devotion, the inner soul — and its treasure of singular devotion. Having given, through the key of his guidance in devotion, all that is his, he has thrown open the veil of maya, of ritual and the rest.

_Shobhaa hai darbaarkee. Prataap Daas Kabir. Panth puraatan khojke. Door kiyaa pad cheer._ (The splendor is that of His court, by the glory of Daas Kabir; having searched out the ancient path, he has torn away and cast off the veil.)

Gnaniji Maharaj says: by the glory of Daas Kabirji the standing of the royal assembly of the Lord's court, the assembly of loving devotion, has grown. He sought out the old, original path of loving devotion and tore away the tattered veil of maya such as ritual.

It is said in the Samagam that Kabir and Narsinh Mehta had one and the same guru, and it has first been explained who and what kind of guru Narsinh Mehta had.

|| Godi ||

_Bhai re mune Hari gaavaani (bhajavaani) tev padi. Maaharaa Shaamaliaane na mooku ek ghadi. Ghailun man maaharun alagu rahi na shake re. Maahare saachi Harisu preet jadi. ||tek|| ||1||_ (O brother, I have grown so used to worshipping Hari that I shall not leave my dark-hued Lord even for a moment. My maddened mind cannot bear to stay apart even an instant — my love has truly become fused with Hari.)

_Aakhaa divasno rali khapi aavyo. Bhaabhiye naa mookyun paani. Men jaanyun tun veranaa maari. Bhaabhi notaa goraani. ||2||_ (Having spent the whole day occupied in worldly business, I came home, but my sister-in-law did not give me water for my bath. I understood: you are indeed my adversary, sister-in-law, not truly a gentle lady.)

_Men jaanyun Dhruvni pere karu re. Naamdevjinaa chhaapraa chhaahi aapyaan. Kabirjine apichal vaani. Evun jaani rose bhataano. Mune chhabilaji mookse paani. ||3||_ (I resolved to do as Dhruv did. He who thatched Namdevji's roof, and gave Kabirji everlasting speech of devotion — knowing this, I grew angry, resolved that my beautiful Lord too will surely give me water,)

_Te pe hun hoees bhalero._ (and thereby I too shall become blessed.)

_Evaan vachan suni Narsaiyaanaan. Bhaabhi bolyaan vaani. Uthho devariaa hun suti huti. Tatkshan mahelyun paani. ||4||_ (Hearing such words from Narsaiya, the sister-in-law spoke: "Get up, brother-in-law, I was asleep" — and at once she brought water.)

_Ghan Vrindaavan ghan Jamunaa tar. Dhan Raadhaa Rukmini raani. Dhan dhan Narsaiyaani jeebhaladi. Je jape chhabilaa Saarang paani. ||5||_ (Blessed is Vrindavan, blessed the bank of the Yamuna; blessed is Queen Radha, blessed Rukmini. Blessed, blessed is Narsaiya's tongue, which chants the name of the beautiful Sarangpani.)

_Kathan kaaraj mune bhaabhiye deedhun. Reesaai gayo van mojhaar. Ugra tap men vanmen saadhyo. Dayaa kari mane Tripuraari. ||6||_ (My sister-in-law set me a hard task; angered, I went off into the forest. There I performed severe austerity, and Tripurari showed me mercy.)

_Gopeshware kahun Narsaiyaa. Je maage te aapo tune. Men kahun prabhu tamne vahalu. Kriyaa karine aapo mune. ||7||_ (Gopeshwar said, "Narsaiya, ask, and whatever you ask I shall grant you." I said, "O Lord, whatever is dear to You — grant that to me, in true act.")

_Bholaa chakravat prasann thayaa. Tatkshan aavi graho haath. Sol sahasra gopivar ramataa. Te raas dekhaadyo jyaan Vaikunthnaath. ||8||_ (The innocent, discus-bearing Lord was pleased, and at once came and took hold of my hand. He showed me the raas-dance where the Lord of Vaikuntha sported among sixteen thousand chief gopis.)

_Shri Vrajbhaanu Nandlaalaa. Sakhi samaani sarve saath. Param kripaal dayaal heet kaaran. Deepak dharaabyo maare haath. ||9||_ (Radha, daughter of Vrajbhanu, was with Nandlal, together with all the gopi companions. The supremely gracious, merciful Lord, for love's sake, placed a lamp in my hand.)

_Het kari mune deekshaa deedhi. Kripaanaath Lakshmi bharathaar. E re Narsaiyaa tun leelaa gaaje. Je keedhi Krishna avataar. ||10||_ (Out of love He gave me initiation — the merciful Lord, husband of Lakshmi. "O Narsaiya, now proclaim the divine play that I performed in the Krishna incarnation.")

Ah, brother, I have grown so used to worshipping the Lord that now I shall not let go of my devotion to Krishna even for one moment. My mind has become so restless that it cannot bear separation from your devotion even slightly. My love has truly become fused with the Lord. One day, after being occupied all day with worldly business, I came home, and my sister-in-law did not give me water for my bath. I thought: this one, who ought to hold me in the highest love, is not behaving like a real sister-in-law but like a guru's wife truly teaching me a lesson. I thought: let me too, like Dhruvji did when he was humiliated, perform such devotion. The Lord who thatched Namdevji's roof, and who gave Kabirji the excellent gift of devotional speech — hymn, kirtan, couplet — understanding that the Lord is such a gracious giver, I grew angry, thinking that the beautiful Lord will give water to me too, and thereby I shall be blessed. Hearing such words from my Narsaiya, my sister-in-law spoke thus: "O my brother-in-law, I was only being neglectful, I was speaking carelessly" — and she at once brought water. Blessed is Vrindavan, blessed is the bank of the river Yamuna, and blessed too are Radhaji and Rukmini; blessed too is the tongue of Narsinh Mehta, which performs such devotion, which recites this hymn and kirtan of devotion to the beautiful Lord.

My sister-in-law spoke harsh words to me, so, angered, I went off into the forest; there I performed nine days of severe, intense austerity, and Shivji showed mercy on me. Gopeshwar Mahadev said, "O Narsinh Mehta, whatever is dear to you, ask it of me graciously." The innocent, good Lord Krishna, bearer of the Sudarshan discus, was pleased, and at once took hold of my hand — that is, called me to Him — and showed me the raas dance being played by the Lord, the very husband of sixteen thousand gopi-queens. Radha, daughter of Vrishabhanu, was there with Nanda's son Krishna, along with all the other gopi companions. That most excellent, gracious Lord, in order to show me mercy, made me hold a lamp in my hand and showed me the raas, and said to me, "O Narsinh, now describe and sing in kirtan what I have shown you — the very sport I performed at the time of my Krishna incarnation."

Narsinh Mehta received just one rebuke from his sister-in-law, and through it was granted the vision of the Lord's raas; he had performed austerity with true inner sincerity and thereby pleased Gopeshwar. This shows that when a person is deeply struck by such a rebuke, and cultivates intense feeling through lament, and becomes resolutely determined to accomplish the task, then his boat crosses over — his task succeeds. Adhyaruji says that if we, in this same way, become firmly resolved and take the Lord's name with true intent, performing devotion, then we shall attain God. If one does not take the Lord's name with dread and intense fervor, calling on His name, how then can the Lord be pleased? There have been many such instances where people, roused by just one such rebuke, attained God or accomplished their task.

Bhaktimarg, Year 1, Issue 1, page 186, 1-28: It is said that when Tulsidas's wife saw Tulsidas maddened after her, she gave him a rebuke:

_Haad chaam may deh mam, taam par jitni preeti. Tisu aadhi jo Raam prati, avasi mitahi bhavbheeti._ ("As much love as you bear for this body of mine, made of bone and flesh — if you bore even half of that for Shri Ramchandra, all the fear of this worldly existence would surely vanish.")

O lord, this decaying, unclean body of flesh and bone — the love you hold for it, if you were to hold even half of that love for Shri Ramchandraji, then every trace of fear of this world would be destroyed — because of this, Tulsidas became a great devotee of Ram.

2. The great devotee of Shri Krishna, Surdas, too, was once caught in infatuation for a courtesan named Chintamani. Then Chintamani herself gave him just such a rebuke: that just as he day and night meditated only on her, and did not even care for his body in seeking to attain her, in the very same way, if he meditated on the Supreme Being with a single mind, and did not care even for his life in doing so, his liberation would come about easily. Surdasji's eyes, which had been asleep in infatuation, were opened by this rebuke, and he became absorbed wholly in devotion to Lord Krishna.

3. The child-devotee Dhruvji, too, was awakened by just such a rebuke from his stepmother: "O son, in this very birth you shall not be able to sit on your father's lap, for you are the son of an unfortunate woman; only if you perform devotion and take birth from my own womb will you become entitled to sit on your father's lap." By this rebuke, at the mere age of five, performing austerity for just six months, he pleased Lord Vishnu and obtained a long reign of royal happiness and the imperishable abode.

4. Narsinh Mehta, too, pleased the Lord through just such a rebuke.

5. A wealthy merchant of Bengal was standing on his porch one evening to buy milk. While taking milk from the milkmaid, he fell into some conversation. The milkmaid gave him a rebuke: "Sheth, you seem to be idle. Just look at the day — the sun is about to set, and I still have far to go." It occurred to him: "Must I too go far, to the other world, and how much longer is it before my own sunset, my own death, comes?" So he left there and went to Vrindavan. There, with his own wealth, he built a temple and lived there performing bhajan; that temple, called Lala Babu's temple, still exists today.

There is also another folk-tale about him: that boatmen on the far bank of the Hooghly river, calling out to people to cross into the city, would shout that evening was falling and this was the very last trip they would take with the boat, so anyone wishing to cross should get in now. By this same rebuke, the temple he had built still exists today as well.

6. A similar incident is that of Saprū Sahib, the English Collector of Itarsi. The barber who used to massage his feet told him a tale: that in the kingdom of Balkh, a maidservant once fell asleep on the king's bed, for which she was sentenced to a hundred lashes. The maidservant said, "I slept on the bed for only ten minutes, and for that a hundred lashes fell on me — then how many would fall on one who sleeps on it permanently?" By this rebuke, that very king became a fakir. Hearing this tale, Collector Saprū too became a sadhu, and came to live in the city of Itawa as a wandering mendicant.

When he grew old, he would go out begging with a stick, and the tapping sound of the stick made a "khat-khat" noise, so people called him "Khatkhata Baba."

7. A similar incident occurred at the death, on the battlefield, of Uday Mehta, the minister of Siddharaj. This Uday Mehta was a Jain; when wounded, he expressed his final wish to have the darshan of a yati (Jain monk). Where could a yati be found on a battlefield? But a soldier brought along an acquaintance, a folk-actor, having dressed him in the garb of a yati. That folk-actor-turned-yati said "Dharma labh," and thereby Uday Mehta's wish was fulfilled, and he died content. Because of this, that folk-actor became, permanently, a true yati.

8. The poet Kalidas was a great fool. Once, a king's son fell ill on the way to his wedding, so in his place an ordinary man had to be made the bridegroom; thus the handsome but foolish Kalidas was made the counterfeit groom. In the bedchamber, the learned princess to whom he had been married, wishing to make sweet conversation with him, asked Kalidas whether he had any words of wit and charm. By this rebuke, Kalidas performed worship of the Goddess Mother and became a great scholar, writing three great epic poems on those very three words, and thus turned from a great fool into a great scholar.

9. Panini, too, was a great fool, so his teacher called him a bullock. So he went and sat by the bull-image in a temple of Shiva, and pleased Shiva, and became a great scholar; he wrote the famous Sanskrit grammar.

10. This is from my own life's experience. I went to Radhnathbhai Laldas of Dhoda, who, together with Trikam Gordhan, had published a garba-book named "Bhakt Bhavamrut" that criticized the revered Yadunathji, to tell him to withdraw it. Radhnathbhai agreed to withdraw it and invited me to dine. I said that just then I had a recitation engagement at the home of devotee Parag Vrundavan of Kandevar in Bodeli Gin, so I had to eat there, but that tomorrow, on my way back, I would eat at his place. Tempted by wanting to secure the book, I went to Dhoda, but through Trikam's persuasion Radhnathbhai changed his mind and refused to withdraw the book; then I refused to eat there. His younger brother Haribhai Laldas urged me not to go hungry; I said I would not even drink water in this village that day. He then invited me to eat at his own home, but I still refused; at that he spoke a couplet:

_Sant bade paramaarthi. Shitam jinkaa ang. Orokee tapat boojhaayke. De de apnaa rang._ (Great saints are ones devoted to others' good, whose very bodies are cool; quenching others' burning heat, they give of their own coolness.)

By this rebuke I softened, and went and ate at Haribhai's home, and then returned home. The meaning is that just one such rebuke is enough to awaken a person; many such instances occur in this world. Draupadi's rebuke — "the blind man's son is blind" — led, among other things, to the Mahabharata war.

Narsinh Mehta reached, in devotion, as high a rank as possible as master of the palace, counting his own sister-in-law as his guru. Now, who Kabirji's guru is has been shown through Kabirji's own composition.

|| Raag Prabhaati ||

_Men (us) daure jaaungaa. To men bohor na bhavjal aaungaa. ||men daure|| ||tatek||_ (I shall go to that chosen place; then I shall never again come into this ocean of worldly existence.)

_Soot bohot kachhu thoraa. Taathe kanthaa laai le doraa. Us laaelau kanth horaa. Kanthaa (su) doraa laagaa. (Tab) taathe jaraa maran bhay bhaagaa. ||men daure|| ||1||_ (Thread — some much, some little — with it, take up the patchwork quilt and stitch it. That quilt has been given whole. Once the thread has caught in the quilt, then the fear of old age and death flees from it.)

_Sannihit puni tahaan kanthaa sanahee poonee. Taanhaan base ek muni. Us munisu man lagaaugaa. To men bohor na bhau jal aaungaa. ||2||_ (There, close by the quilt, lies the carded cotton-thread; there dwells a sage. I shall fix my mind on that sage; then I shall never again come into the waters of worldly existence.)

_Meru dand ek chhaajaa. Taanhaan raaj karat (basat) ek raajaa. Us raajaasun chit laaungaa. To men bohor na bhav jal aaungaa. ||3||_ (The spinal column stands there like a single canopy; there a king reigns. I shall fix my heart on that king; then I shall never again come into the waters of worldly existence.)

_Taanhaan soor na ooge chandaa. Taanhaan dekhaa ek aanandaa. Us aanandsu chit lagaaungaa. Taathe men bohor na bhavjal aaungaa. ||4||_ (There neither sun nor moon rises; there I saw only bliss. I shall fix my heart on that bliss; then I shall never again come into the waters of worldly existence.)

_Taanhaan bahu heeraa dhan motee. Taanhaan tattva laai le joti. Taanhaan base prem joti. Us jotsu jot meelaaungaa. Taathe me bohor na bhavaanal aaungaa. ||5||_ (There are many precious jewels, wealth, pearls; there the light of the essential truth has been brought; there dwells the light of love. I shall merge my light with that light; then I shall never again come into the fire of worldly existence.)

_Ek Triveni trat teeraa. Taanhaan adhar amoolak heeraa. Us heerasu het laaungaa. Taathe men bohor na bhavjal aaungaa. ||6||_ (There is one bank of the Triveni confluence; there hangs an unsupported, priceless jewel. I shall fix my love on that jewel; then I shall never again come into the waters of worldly existence.)

_Taanhaan mool tattva ek paavaa. Taanhaan seedh Ganes rahaavaa. Us moole moole melaaungaa. Taathe men bohor na bhavjal aaungaa. ||7||_ (There the one root essence has been found; there the perfected sages and Ganesh dwell. I shall merge root with root there; then I shall never again come into the waters of worldly existence.)

_Kabir taalab teraa. Taathe (taanhaan) gop Hari guru meraa. Men (us) heet (su) Hari chit laaungaa. Taathe men bohor na bhavjal aaungaa. ||8||_ (Kabir, that is your quest; there the cowherd Hari is my guru. I shall fix my heart on that Hari out of love; then I shall never again come into the waters of worldly existence.)

Daas Kabirji says: I shall go, with single-minded resolve, to such an excellent, firmly determined place, and then I shall not come again and again, taking birth in the four wombs, into the waters of this world's ocean of existence. With the little thread of remembrance that I have, I shall stitch it into the patchwork quilt of loving devotion and sew it up. Once the thread of remembrance and worship has been stitched into this quilt of loving devotion, the fear of birth, old age, and death has departed. There, near the quilt of devotion, dwells a holy saint; I shall fix my mind on that saint, and therefore I shall not come again and again into the waters of this world's ocean of existence. The spinal column serves there as a chief support, like a central pole, where a fitting single essence pervades; there a king rules the kingdom of Ram. If I fix my heart on the loving devotion of that king, I shall not come again and again into the water of birth-and-death of this ocean of existence.

In His abode neither sun nor moon rises, but there is only the happiness of the bliss of loving devotion. If I fix my mind on such bliss of loving devotion, I shall not need to come again and again into this water of birth-and-death of the ocean of existence. In that abode there are great saint-devotees, precious like diamonds and pearls, where the light of the essence of loving devotion has been brought and shines. I too shall join my own loving devotion with that light of loving devotion, and therefore I shall not need to come again and again into this water of birth-and-death of the ocean of existence. There is a bank where the confluence of the tilak, the tulsi, the company of saints, and the Lord's name flows as a stream of loving devotion; and beneath that stream lies the very precious jewel of the Lord's name; I shall fix my mind on that jewel of the Lord's name, and so I shall not need to come again and again into this water of birth-and-death of the ocean of existence.

There, I found the root, the fundamental principle at the origin of this creation, in which perfected beings, Ganesh and other gods, indeed all souls, dwell under its shelter. I shall merge my own root soul-essence with that root divine essence, and so I shall not need to come again and again into this water of birth-and-death of the ocean of existence. Kabirji says: O Kabir, you have such an intense yearning, a longing, to search out and attain this excellent place, and so the cowherds and cowherdesses, and the Lord, are my gurus. I shall lovingly fix my heart upon them, and so I shall not need to come again and again into this water of birth-and-death of the ocean of existence.

Bhaktamaal, Part 2, page 55, in the account of Vrindavan Sudama Kuti, this same theme is also mentioned.

Kabir Dasji accepted Shri Swami Ramanandacharyaji as his initiation-guru, and the gopis as his guru of love. As it is said — _Kabiraa taalib toraa. Tahaan gopi Hari guru moraa. (Gohi 31)_ (Kabir, that is your quest — there, the cowherd Hari is my guru) — it is recorded that once Shri Kabiraji was sitting alone on the bank of the Ganga, repeating "Ram Ram." Meanwhile the Lord too was hiding behind a tree, saying "Kabir-Kabir." And why? Then the Lord answered:

_Man aisaa nirmal bhayaa, jaise Gangaaneer. Peechhe peechhe Hari phirai, kahat Kabir Kabir._ ("My mind has become so pure, like the water of the Ganga, that Hari follows behind me, calling out 'Kabir, Kabir.'")

Hearing this, Kabirdasji said—

_Kabiraa Kabiraa kyoon kahe, jaa Jamunaake teer. Ek gopeeke premmen, bahi gaye koti Kabir. Kaisi premras bheeni aki._ ("Why do you call out 'Kabir, Kabir'? Go to the bank of the Yamuna — there, in love for a single gopi, millions of Kabirs have been swept away. How steeped in the nectar of love that is!")

In Manuscript No. 8, page 84, in Sorath-4, it is said regarding Kabir's quest for a guru:

_Neekalankee guru hum paayaare. Jeenai sudhaapanth bataayaa re. Kabiraa taalab teraa. Hari Parabrahm saaheb meraa._ ("I have found a guru utterly without blemish, who has shown me the path of nectar. Kabir, that is your quest — Hari, the Supreme Brahman, is my Master.")

Daas Kabirji says: I have found a guru — the gopis — utterly without blemish, who has shown me the path of the nectar of love's mark. Kabirji had such an intense longing to attain this kind of devotion, and so my worshipped Lord is Hari, the Supreme Brahman, the Supreme Being.

There are many kinds of gurus, so whichever one truly shows devotion is the fitting guru; therefore it has been told in a couplet what kind of disciple a certain kind of guru has, and what kind of guru a certain kind of disciple has.

_Kabir kaamikaa guru kaaminee. Lobheekaa guru daam. Kabirkaa guru bhagat hai. Bhagatanke guru Raam. ||1||_ (Kabir says: the lustful man's guru is a woman; the greedy man's guru is money. Kabir's guru is the devotee; and the devotee's guru is Ram.)

Daas Kabirji says: the object of worship for the lustful is beauty, and for the greedy it is wealth. Likewise, seekers and the pious are saint-devotees, and the goal of saint-devotees is Ram. Thus people of these three kinds of character — the lustful, the greedy, and the devotee — have gurus according to their own respective nature.

_Kabir trividh lok trigun bhajai. Brahmaa Vishnu Mahesh. Jaisaa guru jaako milai. Sailaa de updesh._ (Kabir says: people of three natures worship the three gunas — Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh. Whatever kind of guru one finds, accordingly he gives his teaching.)

Daas Kabirji says: people with three kinds of nature-traits worship the gods of three kinds of qualities — Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva — that is, they worship these gods possessing the three gunas of sattva, rajas, and tamas. Whoever finds a guru of a particular nature is instructed by him to worship the deity possessing that corresponding quality.

_Gaji mam baasto. Tinko ek got. Jene jevaa gurumale. Taisaa neekasaa pot._ (This is my own experience — theirs is a single lineage: whatever kind of guru one finds, such is the fabric that comes out in the disciple.)

The composer of the couplet says: for me one or another kind of cloth has been prepared — cloth of any kind is still just called cloth, but the cloth that it [text ends here at the close of the section].

sections.title_translit: Karmakandrahit Uda Vaishnav pragat karya, karma marag mukavi ananya marag Uda Vaishnavono pragat kidho te
sections.title_en: How the Ritual-less Uda Vaishnavs Were Brought Forth — Renouncing the Path of Ritual Action, the Unique Path of the Uda Vaishnavs Was Revealed
sections.translation:
Just as the kind of craftsman-guru one gets to prepare it determines whether the cloth turns out well- or poorly-woven.

In the Samagam, the Omkar (the primal sound) is called the ‘basto’ (the loom-warp cloth). This basto is the garment that binds one in bondage; thus the basto is the body the soul receives. The reckoning of one’s gotra (lineage) follows the tradition of the guru-forefathers one has received, and accordingly one’s ‘pot’ — that is, one’s inherent nature and qualities — is formed.

_Koi puje dev dera, koi puje bam. Jene jeva guru male, tene tevi gam._ (Some worship gods in temples, some worship Mahadev. As one gets a guru, so does one’s inclination become.) Some people worship gods and goddesses in temples, while others worship Mahadev (Shiva). Whatever kind of guru gives a person their teaching, that is the kind of devotional understanding they come to have.

_Ashvah shastram shastram vina vani narashcha nari cha, purushavisheshah prapta bhavantyayogyashcha yogyashcha ||119||_ (A horse, a weapon, a scripture, a veena, speech, man and woman — all become fit or unfit according to the particular person into whose hands they fall.) As stated in Mitrabheda [a section of the Panchatantra], a horse, a weapon, a scripture, a veena, speech, man and woman — all of these become fit or unfit depending on the kind of person into whose hands they fall.

HOW THE RITUAL-LESS UDA VAISHNAVS WERE BROUGHT FORTH — RENOUNCING THE PATH OF RITUAL ACTION, THE UNIQUE PATH OF THE UDA VAISHNAVS WAS REVEALED

Comparing the devotion of Kabirji and Narsinh Mehta from every angle, it has been shown that there is no difference between the two. (1) Both had the same guru — the gopis. (2) The dharma of both is the same — that of unique (ananya), one-pointed loving devotion. If anyone thinks that one of the two is higher and the other lower, it is said that such a person’s fortune is poor — there is no unlucky person worse than him. So from comparing the two, the conclusion reached is this: the enchanting flute-player, the Supreme Lord, is indeed the true God of this creation. In this world, this universe, whatever path of ritual action existed — recitation, austerity, vows and the like, sacrifices and offerings, the path of yoga, and devotion to the anadev (minor deities) — Jivanji had all of this given up, and he revealed the path that the unique Vaishnavs were to follow, the path of Satguru Namdev-Kabirji. Through this path, which particular practices of the path of ritual action were made to be given up, that has been shown. (3) The natural disposition (sahaj) of both is the same. (What is called the natural disposition of the gopis — Narsinh Mehta is just like the gopis, because he gave up his masculine identity; hence the natural disposition of the gopis is the same as the natural disposition of Narsinh Mehta.)

On this path, everyone was made a unique (ananya) Vaishnav in a single stroke. What was thereby prohibited from the path of ritual action is stated below.

1. No austerity (tap). 2. No pilgrimage (tirth). 3. No vows (vrat). 4. No yoga. 5. No sacrificial worship (yajan) — no keeping of vigils (jagaran). 6. No vow-offerings (manat) — that is, no keeping of vows of silence, no keeping of religious pledges, or tying a rakhi on the hand. 7. No offering of arghya (ritual water-offering). 8. No study or teaching of the Vedas. 9. No homa (fire-oblation). 10. No yagna (sacrifice). 11. No ritual action (karmakand). 12. Only the practice of devotion (bhakti) is to be done — not devotion to the anadev, but one-pointed, unique devotion alone. 13. Of the four things — tilak, tulsi, the Name of Ram, and the company of saints — one should gather only their essence, the finest part. As for the six systems of philosophy — Nyaya, Vaisheshik, Sankhya, Yoga, Purva Mimamsa (ritual action) and Uttara Mimamsa (Vedanta) — these are not to be pursued. 14. Marriage: without consulting any auspicious moment (muhurta), the bride and groom are to be married in a svayamvar, in the manner of Janak — that is, through the Prithvi Vivah (Earth-Wedding hymn).

In my commentary on the chapter of the Unique (Ananya) Devotee, I noted that this chapter falls roughly in the middle portion of the Samagam. In it, Jivanji Maharaj gave the clarification about Ramkabir’s Name of God, and that Name of God stands at the centre. Now comes the chapter about how the path of the Uda Vaishnavs was revealed as unique devotees — this chapter is like the heart of the Samagam. In it, one is to hold the above-mentioned 14 points inwardly with the oxygen — the life-breath — of Ramkabir, and through this oxygen, exhale out the carbon dioxide, the toxic breath, of the 14-point path of ritual action, so as to make one’s devotion pure and unblemished. Action (karma) exists in everyone, but the dharma of loving devotion (prem bhakti) is actionless (nishkarma). This Vishnu-devotion — the essence of essences, the finest of the finest in the universe — is what the Uda Vaishnavs have practised.

[Note on point 5, yajan: ‘yajan’ means having a sacrifice performed by others on one’s behalf, while ‘ijya’ means performing the sacrificial rites oneself.]

(Bhagavati Katha, Part 8, page 158, note on point 9, homa:) _Hom samast ved yagyamay hi hai. Sadharantaya yagya ka arth hai devatao ke liye dravya ka tyag karna. Ve yagya do prakar ke hote hain, yagya aur hom, jisme khade hokar havan karte hain aur antme vashatkar ka prayog hota hai, unki sangya yaag sangya hai, aur jinme baithkar havan kiya jata hai aur antme swaha ka prayog hota hai tatha jo yajya aur puronuvakya se rahit hote hain use hom kahte hain._ (Homa is entirely of the nature of Vedic sacrifice. Generally, ‘yajna’ means giving up material substance for the deities. Such sacrifices are of two kinds — yajna and homa. Those performed standing, ending with the utterance ‘vashat’, are called ‘yaag’; those performed sitting, ending with ‘swaha’, and lacking the yajya and puronuvakya formulas, are called ‘homa’.)

In ancient times there was a custom of holding a svayamvar. The bride’s relatives would invite all the kings for the svayamvar. When the kings arrived, the bride’s companions would describe the qualities of each one. Having seen and heard of their form and virtues, the bride would then place the wedding garland on the one she desired, after which the marriage would be performed with due rites. The svayamvars of Sita, Draupadi, Indumati and other such brides are illustrations of this. The custom of svayamvar existed ages ago, but Jivanji Maharaj conceived of a wedding practice of similarly excellent character and began an excellent tradition — marrying without consulting any auspicious moment — in a manner equal to the svayamvar. To have run the marriage tradition through the hymn of the Prithvi Vivah (Earth-Wedding), without Vedic ritual, is how great a revolution this is. The 14 prohibited points of the Uda Vaishnavs are Jivanji Maharaj’s forceful movement against anadev-worship and ritual action — and not only that, he had it put into practice in ordinary society, where it remains alive and unchanged to this day. The mention of the wedding canopy (sadhara mandap) is given in the Prithvi Dhol wedding hymn, and the hymn has been composed in such a way that the rite of marriage is performed while holding such excellent, meaning-filled, ideal thoughts. This shows Adhyaruji Maharaj’s devotion of feeling.

The practice of the muhurta was introduced later by the Brahmins. It is written in the Nigam Prakash that in ancient times people did not determine an auspicious moment for marriage, as is evident from the Ashvalayana and Baudhayana Sutras.

_Sarvakalam eke vivaham_ — Ashvalayana (Marriage may take place at any time.) _Sarvaprashasta vivahasya_ — Baudhayana (Every occasion is fit for marriage.)

_Surya-chandrau mangalash cha, budhash chapi Brihaspatih, shukrash cha shanish charo Rahuh, ketush cheti graha nava._ (Sun and Moon, Mars, Mercury, and also Jupiter, Venus and Saturn, Rahu, and Ketu — these are the nine planets.) Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, Rahu, and Ketu — these are the nine planets (grahas). Ketu is the comet, the ‘tailed star’.

_Narsinh naam bal bhajanko, tahe navgrah kya kare. Rahu Ketu Ravi Chandra, sada bhaktanke hetu. Sad sati na sanchare, buddhi anandko dani. Sada hot kalyan, kalyan kalyani. Vidhan haran mangal karan, Agradaske ur pad dhare. Narsinh naam bal bhajanko, tahe navgrah kya kare._ (By the strength of chanting the Name ‘Narsinh’, what can the nine planets do to him? Rahu, Ketu, the Sun, the Moon and the rest exist always for the good of the devotees. Not even the seven-and-a-half-year affliction [sadesati] touches him; the Name is the giver of right understanding and supreme bliss — it ever brings only well-being upon well-being. It removes obstacles and brings good fortune; Agradas holds its feet enshrined in his heart. By the strength of chanting the Name ‘Narsinh’, what can the nine planets do to him?) For practising devotion to God, the divine Name ‘Narsinh’ is exceedingly excellent. Whoever chants and worships taking this Name, the nine planets can do him no harm at all. Rahu, Ketu, the Sun, the Moon and the other planets are always working for the welfare of God’s devotees. Not even the sadesati — the seven-and-a-half-year affliction — can touch them. God, the giver of right understanding and supreme bliss, is always the well-wisher and benefactor of His devotees. Agradas holds in his heart the devotion of the God who removes the devotees’ obstacles and difficulties and who does good, auspicious things for them. How, then, could the nine planets ever afflict one who sings and chants this divine Name, Narsinh? They simply cannot.

Adhyaruji Maharaj too points to this divine Name ‘Narsinh’. This form of Narsinh is that in which God is the slayer of whoever torments His devotee.

_Parbrahm name mandal purawo, sumran Narsinh vir baulawo._ (Fill the sacred circle with the Name of the Supreme Brahm; invoke, through remembrance, the valiant Narsinh.) God assumes the form of Narsinh as a mighty, glorious manifestation. It further says,

_Shri Padmanabh Parbrahm em maliya, chhutya re sat lakh kod, chhutya re jantu prani avatarna e, ho Narhar, chhutya re._ (Thus we met Shri Padmanabh, the Supreme Brahm — released, O released, are hundreds of thousands and crores of births; released, O released, from taking birth as creatures and animals, O Narhar — released, O released.) The Supreme Brahm, as Lord Padmanabh, has now graced us in such a way that, by His manifestation, the sorrows of our hundreds of thousands and crores of births have ended, and taking birth in the bodies of the eighty-four lakh species of creatures and animals has come to an end. O Lord, having come now and met us as Lord Narsinh-Padmanabh, our hundreds of thousands and crores of births and rebirths have thus ceased.

Thus the Laghuras hymn has been composed giving importance to God’s Narsinh form, with ‘Narsinh’ as its refrain (dhruvpad). By the strength of the divine Name, the devotee does not fear the nine planets or afflictions such as the sadesati.

_Tulsi Raghubar dahena, sabai dahena tahe. Lagan muhurat shubh ghadi, Tulsi gane na kahe._ (Says Tulsi[das]: whoever has the Lord Raghubar’s right hand of favour upon him has everything favourable to him; Tulsi reckons no auspicious moment, hour, or occasion as necessary for him.) Tulsidas says that one upon whom God’s grace rests like His mighty right hand has, for that reason, the utmost grace of all the powers of the world. Hence such people, who live wholly by grace, hold no fear of the wheel of planets or the zodiac for marriage, nor of auspicious hours or moments; they pay no heed to muhurtas or the like for marriage. Devotees of God remain so intoxicated, so absorbed, in the rasa of loving devotion, that they take no account even of the most arrogant or powerful of people.

_Bhakt bawle gyani alhad, yogi bade nikhattu, karmakandi aise dole, jyon bhadeka tattu._ (Devotees appear mad, the wise appear carefree, great yogis appear useless and idle; ritualists roam about like a hired pack-horse.)
