(Nine lakh species born in water, ten lakh species of birds, thirty lakh cow-and-kindred creatures, twenty lakh immobile species, eleven lakh crawling insects, and four lakh human beings — only after crores of such births are gone through does one obtain the rare human body.)

Of beings born in water there are nine lakh species; ten lakh species of birds; thirty lakh species of cows and the like; twenty lakh species of immobile beings; eleven lakh species of crawling insects; and four lakh human beings — among these, only after passing through crores of such births does one obtain the rare human body.

The Gita, chapter 9, verse 21, says:

_Te tam bhuktva svargalokam vishalam_
_kshine punye martyalokam vishanti,_
_Evam trayidharmamanupraapanna_
_gatagatam kamakama labhante. ||21||_
(Having enjoyed that vast heavenly realm, when their merit is exhausted, they enter the mortal world once more; thus those who follow the threefold Vedic path, desiring the objects of desire, obtain only a repeated coming and going.)

Having enjoyed that vast heavenly realm, when their merit runs out, they attain the human world once more — thus, those who take refuge in the desire-driven path of the Vedas, and who long for sense-objects, merely come and go again and again.

The Bhagavat, canto 11, chapter 10, verse 26, says:

_Tavat pramodate svarge, yavat punyam samapyate,_
_Kshinapunyah patatyarva ganichchhan kalachalitah. ||26||_
(He enjoys pleasure in heaven only until his merit is exhausted; then, his merit spent, driven by time, he falls back down against his will.)

As long as his merit is not exhausted, that meritorious man goes on enjoying pleasure in this way; then, when his merit runs out, driven onward by time, he falls back down, even though he has no wish to do so.

(A kavit-rekhta:)

_Nav lakh jalmein jiv, das pankhi parvara, ektalis lakh kramkit,_
_Vis sathavar vistara, char lakh manakh vadhani tattvaveta trihi,_
_Lokmein char lakh sacharachar, sab jivanmein dhanya jiv hai je samer dharani dhara._
(Nine lakh beings live in water, ten lakh among the birds, forty-one lakh crawling insects, twenty lakh spread among the immobile species, and four lakh forms of humankind, so say the knowers of truth. In the world there are, in all, eighty-four lakh species of the moving and unmoving — and among all living beings, blessed is that being who bears the burden of the earth.)

The original Samagam's pages 305-306 are missing; on what remains of page 306, the last half of verse 78 reads as follows: "...ti divyamana tam eva sharanagata" — meaning: O Supreme Being of divine radiance, your devotees come to your refuge. The commentary on this verse is as follows:

Commentary: those nine lakh forms of incarnation in water, ten lakh forms as birds, eleven lakh forms as crawling insects, thirty lakh forms as immobile beings, twenty (thirty) lakh forms as cows and other such creatures, and four lakh forms as human beings — through these, by chance, one may be born, attain a kingdom and enjoy it; may perform sacrifices; may ascend to the throne of Indra; may again become lodged in the tree; may again fall to the mortal world — these are the entanglements, the hardships one wanders through. But having gone through all this, if one comes to take refuge in a Guru, then all karma is dispelled. This is the 46th verse of the Pandava Gita:

_Go kotidanam grahaneshu Kashiprayaga-Gangayutakalpavasah,_
_Yajnayutam meru-suvarnadanam Govindanamna na kadapi tulyam. ||79||_
(The gift of crores of cows during an eclipse, ten thousand kalpas of residence at Kashi, Prayag, and on the banks of the Ganga, ten thousand sacrifices, and the gift of gold equal to Mount Meru — none of this can ever equal the name of Govind.)

The gift of crores of cows at the time of an eclipse, ten thousand kalpas of dwelling at Kashi, Prayag, and the banks of the Ganga, ten thousand yajnas, and the gift of gold equal in weight to Mount Meru — all of this together can never equal the one name of the Supreme Lord.

(Parashuram's kavit:)

_Kapil dhen jaltar, kot jo Ganga tirath nahave,_
_Vipra taran pargar, pokh de bhalo manave,_
_De gaj gahvar dan, bhom dohari manave,_
_Kanak patra de soparna, chir tokha pahanave,_
_Ashvamegh jagan kare, kot kanya parnave,_
_Turi aan palan, khandh de aap chadave,_
_Kiyo na mite Keshava, Farasram Govind bin._
(Even if one worships the tawny cow, bathes in the waters of crores of Ganga pilgrimage sites, washes the feet of Brahmins and lovingly provides for their nourishment, secretly gives away elephants in charity, gives gifts of land, gives golden plates and jewelled ornaments, dresses recipients in fine bright garments, performs the Ashwamedha sacrifice, gives away crores of maidens in marriage, brings a fine horse fully saddled and mounts and offers it himself — Parashuram says, O Keshava, none of this deed is undone without devotion to Govind.)

Parashuram says: one who worships the dusky-hued cow, bathes in the waters of crores of pilgrimage sites of the Ganga, washes the feet of Brahmins and takes delight in nourishing them well, secretly gives away elephants in charity, gives away two pieces of land, gives gold-plated gifts and dresses recipients in bright garments, performs the Ashwamedha sacrifice, gives away crores of maidens in marriage, brings the full trappings for a horse and mounts and decorates it himself and gives it away — even so, whatever deeds one has done, without devotion to God, however many such religious observances one performs, deliverance will not come.

_Dayala Harki ehi van hai, je harijanke bas hoy,_
_Kot jagan jo koi karo, pan harijan tyan Hari hoy. ||10||_
(Merciful is this word spoken by Hari himself — that he remains under the sway of his devotees; even if someone performs crores of sacrifices, Hari still dwells only wherever his true devotees are.)

This is a word spoken by God's own mouth: that he remains under the control of his Harijans; therefore, even if someone performs crores of sacrifices, God remains present only where his Harijans, his devotees, are.

The fruit of one's merit cannot be erased even by Keshav-Krishna himself. Therefore the merit earned through giving cows, pilgrimage, gifts to Brahmins, the Ashwamedha sacrifice, the gift of maidens, and the like, cannot be erased — it must be experienced. But if instead you sing the praises and glories of Govind, such a result will not come about.

Kabirji stirred up a revolution against the forces that deceive and disrupt devotion to Vishnu through fraud, but nothing came of it in the end. Yet our true Guru, Jivanji, without holding back out of shame, boldly and courageously exposed these forces, and it is this exposure that has been presented in this Samagam. It has shown how the soul is prevented from crossing over by the confusion of maya and Brahma:

1. Through the confusion of maya and Brahma, the soul cannot cross over.
2. Through the thirteen-and-a-half kandas of the Yajurveda, there remains a confusion between devotion and liberation, so the soul cannot attain the Supreme Lord.
3. The unbroken divine play of Vasudev cannot be perceived, through the Guru's grace, by one who has not attained it.
4. Jivanji came for the welfare and salvation of the soul.
5. "If one, freed from the bondage of the three states caused by the three gunas — birth, death, and old age — worships Me, one attains the nectar of My liberation and is delivered."
6. Unless one is freed from the deception of the ten incarnations, the soul cannot attain the Supreme Lord.
7. Without devotion to Vishnu, the Supreme Reality cannot be attained; the eighty-eight thousand sages, the thirty-three crore deities, and Brahma and others are all turned away from Vasudev, hostile to devotion to Vishnu — the righteousness of Govind will not appear to them.
8. In Aryavarta, in the Kali age, such Vaishnavas will appear that, through the sarshti kind of liberation set in motion by the Sanakadi sages across the three ages, they will attain power and majesty equal to God's own.
9. Vaishnavji revealed the path of liberation-while-living.
10. Unless the true form of a saint is understood, how can one attain the Supreme Lord?
11. If the Honest-Looking Thief keeps circling around one's devotion to Vishnu, the soul cannot cross over.
12. The quarrel that has been set up over the Ashwamedha and similar rites, within devotion to Vishnu, prevents the soul from attaining the Supreme Lord.
13. Finally, it was explained that if the great entanglements — the hardships and obstructions caused by the thief within devotion to Vishnu — are released, then the soul attains the Supreme Lord in this way.

The Honest-Looking Thieves described in the Samagam have been written about in the sakhis of the Garbhavali section.

_Aap vyapak Jivana, tej jot kiya akas,_
_Bin mundka chor hai, sab jag kiya garas. ||3||_
(Self-pervading, O Jivan, Brahman made itself into radiance, light, and sky; this headless thief has devoured the entire world.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: Brahma-radiance, Brahma-light, and the five great elements — fire, light, sky, and the rest — this spontaneous self-pervasion of the unqualified Brahman occurs of its own accord. This Brahman is like a headless thief, a thief without form, and it has swallowed up, devoured, the entire world.

_Aatam parmeshvar pame nahi, Jivana keha vichar,_
_Shahutor aage fire, sohi bade vatpar. ||4||_
(The soul does not attain the Supreme Lord, O Jivan — such is my reflection; whatever keeps circling in front as an "Honest-Looking Thief" — that indeed is the greatest highway robber.)

Devotees, terrified of these wicked thieves, ask Jivandasji Maharaj: O Jivandasji, such cunning thieves of maya have kept circling before our devotion — they alone are the great robbers, and because of them the soul cannot attain the Supreme Being. So please tell us who these thieves are, and what they are like.

_Pahela dash avatar hai, duja Vaikuntha jan,_
_Trijo Omkar Jivana, chotha ghatghat man. ||5||_
(The first is the ten incarnations; know the second to be Vaikuntha; the third, O Jivan, is Omkar; and the fourth is the notion that God is fully present in every single vessel.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: the first Honest-Looking Thief is the ten incarnations; know that the second is Vaikuntha; the third is Omkar; and the fourth thief is the claim that the Supreme Brahman is fully and completely present in every single heart — this too, understand, is a Honest-Looking Thief, as I have told you.

_Panchman Sanakadik hai, chhathi Bhagirathi Ganga,_
_Satmi Ekadashi Jivana, jivkun baura kin. ||6||_
(The fifth is the Sanakadi sages, the sixth is the Bhagirathi Ganga, and the seventh, O Jivan, is Ekadashi — which has driven every living being mad and bewildered.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: the fifth Honest-Looking Thief is the Sanakadi sages, the sixth is the Bhagirathi Ganga, and the seventh is Ekadashi — which has made all living beings mad and utterly bewildered.

_Sat Vishnu bhakti manhi mile, apane pad lai jay,_
_Mota odavada Jivana, Parmeshvar nahi pay. ||7||_
(These seven mingle within devotion to Vishnu, and lead one away to their own respective abodes; great are these entanglements, O Jivan — through them one does not attain the Supreme Lord.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: all these Honest-Looking Thieves mix themselves in under the name of devotion to Vishnu, and then lead us away, each to its own abode; therefore all of them are great entanglements — troubles that, like the trailing end of a sari catching on things, cloak the true practice of devotion to Vishnu with their perverse influence.

_Sapt shahuchor taje, tab Vishnu bhakti ja hoy,_
_Tab hi aatam Jivana, male param pad soy. ||8||_
(Only when one abandons these seven Honest-Looking Thieves does true devotion to Vishnu come about; only then, O Jivan, does the soul attain that supreme state.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: only when one renounces these seven Honest-Looking Thieves can true devotion to Vishnu come about, and only then can the soul attain that true supreme state, the abode of God.

Selfish, cunning thieves infiltrate devotion to Vishnu by deceiving people, joining in through guerrilla-like methods, and corrupt our devotion from within — these thieves have been exposed by Jivanji Maharaj, and he has made us alert so that we may be saved from them. It is written in the Samagam that Jivandasji therefore said: "O brothers, walk with your eyes open — these are the Honest-Looking Thieves of devotion to Vishnu" — and this account has been given, beginning with the first, the ten incarnations, and so on, as Jivandasji

Speaking further of these hidden thieves: knowing the names of these seven thieves is astonishing to everyone, and on hearing their names it might seem that whoever calls such pillars of devotion "thieves" has himself gone astray. But all of them have infiltrated in such a way that everyone takes these thieves to be the very ones granting true devotion — which is exactly why Jivandasji Maharaj calls them shahukar chor ("respectable thief" — a thief who is trusted like an honest merchant). The reasons for this have been shown in the discussion within the satsang (holy gathering/discourse), and at the very end of the satsang their full reckoning has been given. So let us now consider why each of these has been called a thief.

First:

The Ten Avatars — this has been discussed in the Prabodh Anga (chapter), and it is also mentioned in the satsang while discussing the story of Ambarish.

_dash avatarke dagdage | bhulya sab sansar ||
ko ek ugare jivana | jine gurumukh kiyo vichar ||34||_ (Deluded by the flicker of the ten avatars, the whole world has gone astray. Only some rare one is saved, O Jivana, who has reflected through the guru's teaching.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: because God took on the ten avatars in the episode of Ambarish, all the people of the world fell into doubt about devotion to God; but those devotees who had received true understanding from their guru — some rare one among them — were saved from this.

In the satsang, in the chapter on Morli Manohar Parmeshwar (the flute-charming Lord), it is stated that Durvasa's curse was upon Ambarish, and to avert that curse, God agreed to take on the ten avatars in place of Ambarish. So the ten avatars are only names of the forms God assumed; but the God-essence (bhagavat-tattva) that agreed to take the ten avatars is God's original, true form. Therefore it is the Parbrahma God-essence itself, in name and form, that should be worshipped. The names that arose from the forms God took are, as name-forms, illusory (mithya); but the essential Name-Form remains unbroken and eternal.

_avatar aparadhi kahe jivana | jake nahi guru pir ||
aadi ant madhya shamlo | nirgun brahma sharir ||35||_ (Only the sinful offenders, O Jivana, who have no true guru, count God among the avatars. He who is the dark-hued Shyam is present at the beginning, middle, and end — his body is that of the formless, attributeless Brahma.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: it is only those sinful offenders whose guru is not capable who count God among the avatars. But God, who is Parbrahma, beyond the three gunas (qualities of nature), is Himself present before the avatars, after them, and during them as well — and throughout, He was one and the same, the dark-hued Krishna.

_ram krishna je jivana | do sargun avatar ||
andh dhandh kaha bhaju | je ved na pave paak ||36||_ (Ram and Krishna, O Jivana, are the two avatars with attributes (saguna). Why worship blindly in confusion, when even the Vedas cannot fathom them fully?)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: Ram and Krishna are the two saguna (with-attribute) avatars of Parbrahma. But even the Veda-Brahma cannot understand this saguna-nirguna essence — so what need is there to fall into confusion over the saguna-nirguna question regarding Ram and Krishna, who are beyond all attributes (gunatit)?

By this sakhi (couplet), Ram and Krishna are counted among the ten avatars — but that avatar-form of Ram and Krishna is only a glimpse of God's saguna avatar. Indeed, Ram and Krishna are a glimpse of God's saguna avatar; yet Ram and Krishna, both before and after the avatar and even now, remain unbroken in name-form.

_kab raghupati kab jadupati | do sagun avatar ||
bemukh na samajh jivana | ai sab ekakar ||38||_ (Sometimes as Raghupati [Ram, lord of the Raghu clan], sometimes as Jadupati [Krishna, lord of the Yadu clan] — these are the two saguna avatars. Those who are turned away [faithless] do not understand, O Jivana, that all these are one and the same.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: sometimes as Ram and sometimes as Krishna, God takes avatar for the welfare of devotees, but those without this understanding fail to grasp that both these forms belong to the one and same Supreme God.

_dase avatare shamlo | chovise akhand ||
sab sakhiyanma jivana | vyapyo kot brahmand ||38||_ (The dark-hued Lord is present, whole and undivided, in all ten avatars as well as in all twenty-four avatars. He pervades all the gopis, O Jivana, and pervades crores of universes as well.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: Lord Krishna is contained, undivided, in all ten avatars as well as in the twenty-four avatars. That same Krishna pervades all the gopis, and in the same way pervades crores of universes. The God who pervades crores of universes also pervades in the midst of the gopis.

In Krishnadas's Parchari, it is said regarding the avatars of Ram and Krishna:

_ram krishna e puran brahma | ja samarte mite sab karma ||492||
ehi anjan mahe arup | ehi chaud lokko bhuya ||493||_ (Ram and Krishna are the complete Brahma; remembering them erases all karma. They, though within maya, are formless; they are the lords of the fourteen worlds.)

Ram and Krishna are the complete Brahma, the Supreme God. By remembering and worshipping them, all karmic faults and sins are removed. They themselves are the formless Supreme God within saguna maya. Such are they — the ruler-owners of the fourteen worlds.

_ehi sakal srishtike karta | pratipalan sabke harta ||494||
arup anjanme avinashi | avadhpuri vrindavan vasi ||495||_ (They are the creators of all creation, the sustainers and also the destroyers of all. Formless and imperishable within maya, they dwell in Avadhpuri [Ayodhya] and Vrindavan.)

They themselves are the creators of the entire world, the all-powerful ones who nurture and sustain all, and who also destroy all. Formless and imperishable even within saguna maya, they are the very manifest God who resides in Ayodhya and Vrindavan.

Sakhi (couplet):

_kabir ramkrishna avatar kahe | man dhave chatu aur ||
so aparadhi jivku | chaud lok nahi thaur ||46||417||_ (Kabir says: those who call Ram and Krishna mere avatars, whose mind keeps running elsewhere — such offending souls find no place anywhere in the fourteen worlds.)

Das Kabirji says: those who say that Ram and Krishna came by taking avatar, and who keep letting their minds run astray in every direction — such sinful souls will find no salvation anywhere among the fourteen worlds. They will meet with downfall.

Thus Jivandasji, citing Krishnadas as well, has called the ten avatars a shahukar chor (respectable thief).

In Handwritten Manuscript No. 48, page 49, in the 20th verse of "Dadu Panth Parkhyana" (Recognizing the Dadu Path), it is written:

_lokvedka marag taje | manme ek niranjan bhaje |
isht na rakhe das avatar | dadu panthi so niradhar ||20||_ (One who abandons the worldly-Vedic path and worships in the mind the one stainless Lord, and who does not hold the ten avatars as his chosen deity — know for certain that he is a follower of the Dadu path.)

Those who abandon the path of worldly custom and Vedic ritual, and who inwardly hold devotion to the maya-free Parbrahma, and who do not accept the ten avatars as their object of worship — know for certain that such people are followers of the Dadu path. Thus, besides ourselves, the followers of the Dadu path too are in agreement with our view.

_amrikh gohare aaviyo | sundar shyam swarup ||
so nand dware jivana | je dashrath kul badbhup ||22||_ (He who came at Amrikh's [Ambarish's] cry for help, of beautiful dark-hued form — that same one, O Jivana, plays at Nand's door, he who was the great king of Dashrath's lineage.)

Prabodh (chapter):

Jivandasji Maharaj says: the God of beautiful dark-hued form who came at King Ambarish's cry for protection is the very same God who is now sporting in Nandji's courtyard — he who was the great king in the lineage of King Dashrath.

_amrish gohare aaviyo | hari dharmo natvar vesh ||
sab jag bhulyo jivana | karat anek anek ||23||_ (Hari came at Amrish's [Ambarish's] cry for help, wearing the guise of a master performer. The whole world was deceived, O Jivana, seeing him take on so many, many forms.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: God, coming to help King Ambarish, took on the guises of the ten avatars like an actor; because of this, the whole world keeps saying that God is many different beings.

Thus, because of the dazzling illusion of the ten avatars, people fail to grasp the true understanding of God as Ram-Krishna, and so, in the matter of devotion to God, the ten avatars have become like a shahukar chor (respectable thief).

God has 24 principal avatars, of which ten are the main ones: 1. Matsya (fish), 2. Kachchha (tortoise), 3. Varah (boar), 4. Nrusinh (man-lion), 5. Vaman (dwarf), 6. Parashuram, 7. Ram, 8. Krishna, 9. Buddha, 10. Kalki. In the Bhagavat, 22 avatars are listed, in which three avatars — Mohini, Hans, and Hayagriv — are excluded [from that count]; within it, Dhanvantari is counted together with [avatars] 12–13. So here we have called only the ten avatars a shahukar chor, because they are the principal ones. But regarding avatars in general, we do not accept the other avatars either. As for Ram and Krishna, we do not accept them merely as avatar-holders, but accept them as the complete Parbrahma, the Supreme God.

Gnaniji Maharaj writes in the Anahar Anga (chapter):

_pure dharki vanagi | gnani das avatar ||
gnani dhyani muni thako | ved na pave paar ||1||_ (The ten avatars are, O wise one, but a sample of the complete essence. Even wise sages, meditators, and munis have grown weary, and even the Vedas cannot reach its far shore.)

Gnaniji Maharaj says: God's ten avatars are but a kind of sample or fragment of His complete Parbrahma essence. Even great sages (jnanis), yogis who meditate through the path of yoga, and munis have grown weary from trying again and again to gain knowledge of it, and even the Vedas have not been able to know it.

_dariya rupi ram hai | lahar ve avatar |
aadi ant madhya nahi | taka eh vistar ||2||_ (Ram is like the ocean, and the avatars are its waves. This expanse of his has no beginning, middle, or end.)

Gnaniji Maharaj says: God's original, true form is as vast as the ocean, and these avatars of his are merely fragments, like the waves that arise in the ocean. This God-essence has no beginning, middle, or end — and it is from that same God that this expanse, in the form of avatars and in the form of the world, has spread out.

Kabirji has said in the Agadh Anga (chapter):

_kabir dariya rupi ram hai | tarang ve avatar |
dou tarang bich agla | take yah vistar ||8||_ (Kabir says: Ram is like the ocean, and the avatars are its waves; wave following wave, one after another ahead — such is his expanse.)

Das Kabirji says: God's original form is as vast as the ocean, and these avatars are like its waves — just as after two waves rise, a further wave follows, and after that wave another wave arises, in that same way these avatars occur one after another.

At the end of the chapter on "Pret Bhojan" (feeding of ghosts) and the unrighteous devotee, in this sakhi of Kabirji, at the end of the hymn (pad) "Santo Aave Jaaye So Maaya," it is written: _das avatar ishwari maya, taku karta kar bujha_ (the ten avatars are God's maya; understand who its doer/creator is). Thus, worldly people have given great importance to the ten avatars, but in the satsang it has been said that these ten avatars are themselves divine maya.

The ten avatars have made a deep impression on the popular mind. An arati (devotional hymn) has even been composed for them — "Jai Vaikunthadhish..." — and in the Geet Govind, Jaidev has described the ten avatars in verse 1.2.1, which has been placed here as a shlok. In Handwritten Manuscript No. 81, page 66, in the hymn (pad) beginning "Pratham Narayan Machharup Avatariya" ("First, Narayan descended in the form of a fish"), the ten avatars are described.

Among the seven honest-looking thieves, the ten avatars were named first, and Vaikunth is counted second. It will come as a surprise to hear that Vaikunth — the very abode people pine and die for — is called a thief along with the others. These "honest" thieves are called thieves precisely because they appear supreme to the world's unwise people, yet relying on them does not bring about our liberation. So we named the ten avatars as the first thief, but on closer look all seven of these thieves are, in one way or another, counted as avatars themselves. Among the twenty-four avatars, Vaikunth too is counted as an avatar. Besides those twenty-four, other avatars of God are also recognized. Among these, the third thief — Omkar — is counted as an avatar too, regarded as the sound-avatar (nadavatar). The fourth thief, the one dwelling in every heart (ghat-ghat), is the notion "I am Brahman" (aham brahm); a portion of the divine essence resides in every body. The fifth, Sanakadik, is counted among the twenty-four avatars. The sixth is Ekadashi. When God grew angry in order to slay the demon Madhukaitabh, a maiden appeared from that anger, and her name was Ekadashi; thus Ekadashi too is counted as an avatar of God. The seventh is the Ganga, called Vishnu-Padodaki (water from Vishnu's feet). During the Sanakadik avatar — since the Sanakadik sages were themselves an avatar of God — when God's foot struck their sweat-filled water-pot (kamandal), the stream that flowed from it was called the Ganga; thus the Ganga too is counted as part of that same avatar of God.

In the detailed discussion of the seven honest-looking thieves, Omkar, Ekadashi, and Ganga have been explained at length, while Vaikunth, Sanakadik, and the thief dwelling in every heart have only been mentioned in passing. Let us now look at what flaw lies within these. Vaikunth, being renowned as the abode of God, spreads its attraction among people, yet no one recognizes the fault hidden within it.

Vaikunth means the abode of Vishnu, the dwelling place of Vishnu. It is said that in the lower region of Satyalok, Vishnulok, and Golok there lies Vaikunthlok as one of its parts. The spiritual meaning of Vaikunth is that the intellect remains unblunted (akunth) through all religious observances. (Jagdish notebook no. 264, page 293)

Kshirpayonidhi — the Kshirsagar, the ocean of milk. Some scholars also call the Kshirsagar "Shvetdwip" (the White Island). Shvetdwip is the gateway to Vaikunth. Another name for Vaikunth is "Vyapi Vaikunth" (the all-pervading Vaikunth).

In the imperishable, all-pervading Vaikunth, the tree of the Vedas sprouts from the seed of the Pranav (the syllable Om). From this it appears that Brahma, who emerged from the navel-lotus of God reclining in the Kshirsagar, uttered the sound Om, and from that seed the Vedas were composed. This is why we do not accept this Vaikunth possessed of the Omkar-principle.

God's avatar exists in the form of Vaikunth. In the Raivat Manvantar, God took an avatar named "Vaikunth", born from the womb of Vaikuntha, wife of Shubhra. It is said that this same God then created Vaikunthlok. The Bhagavatam, in Canto 8, Chapter 5–6, verse 4, states that the wife of the sage Shubhra was named Vikuntha. From her womb, God himself, through his own portion (amsha), took an avatar named Vaikunth, together with the finest of the gods. Pleased by the prayer of Goddess Lakshmi, he then fashioned the abode of Vaikuntha for her.

Register no. 452, page 73, states that there are 108 Vaikunths on earth, and five other Vaikunths besides.

1. Kshirsagar Vaikunth — _Jab Shrimannarayan nidraki prerna karte hai tab Brahma nidravash swapnavasthako prapt hote hai aur tab Narayanki icchase jagat jalarpan hota hai jise naimitya pralay kahte hai - uska karan Kshirsagar Vaikunth hai_ (When Shrimannarayan induces sleep, Brahma falls into a dream-state under its sway, and by Narayan's will the world is then submerged in water — this is called the naimittika pralaya, incidental dissolution — and its cause is the Kshirsagar Vaikunth.)

2. Ramavaikunth — _jahan Sanakadikne Jay-Vijayko shaap diya tha_ (where Sanakadik cursed Jay and Vijay.)

3. Karan Vaikunth — _jahan mahapralayme prakriti purush samyatako prapt hone hai, jahan teeno gun aur panch tattva sam hai. Jab wahi purush Mahavishnu iccha karte hai tab phir jagat waisa hi ho jata hai_ (where, at the time of the great dissolution, Prakriti and Purush attain equilibrium, where the three gunas and the five elements are in balance; when that same Purush, Mahavishnu, wills it, the world comes into being again just as before.)

Brahma's going to the Kshirsagar with the gods, and praying there for an avatar to be taken — all of this occurs within that one quarter [ekapad] of the Lord's manifested glory. The three-quarter glory [tripad vibhuti] may be reached only by the liberated, through the archiradi path via the sushumna channel. The Kaushitaki Upanishad describes this in detail.)

_Iti sambhashya bhagavan arjunena saheshwarah, divyam swaratham asthaya pratichim disham avishamat_ (Thus having conversed, the Lord, together with Ishwar and Arjun, mounted the divine chariot and set out toward the west) — from here up to verse 57 the earthly Vaikunthdham is described. After this comes the account of the reverent exchange of greetings with the Lord of Vaikunth, the return to Dwarka bearing the brahmin's sons, and Arjun's astonishment at Shri Krishna's glory. This Vaikunth lies beyond the Lokalok mountain, beyond darkness, above the pure waters.

_Ramavaikunth ke dwarke sameep Dhruvjika nivas sthal hai - Atha tasmat paratah trayodasha-laksha-yojanantaro yat tad Vishnoh paramam padam abhivandati yatraha mahabhagvato Dhruva_, and so on (Near the gate of Ramavaikunth lies the dwelling place of Dhruvji — "Beyond that, at a distance of thirteen lakh yojanas, lies that supreme abode of Vishnu, which the great devotee Dhruv reverently worships.")

In the Bhagavatam, Canto 8, first half, in the account of the Raivat Manvantar, verses 4–5 and others make it clear that Lord Vaikunth, son of Vikuntha, manifested Ramavaikunth at the prayer of Lakshmiji. The going there of the Sanakadik brahmarshis, and their cursing of Jay and Vijay, is the story of Ramavaikunth.

Register no. 449, page 49, states:

_Vishnu avatarse Vaikunth Dham, Shrimannarayanavatarse Kshirshayi Vaikunth aur paratpar Parabrahm Samavatarse Saket Dham. According to the doctrine of the Agam Samhitas, Vaikunth is called the highest heaven, and in Vaikunth one attains sayujya — union of identity with God.)

Thus, among the four kinds of liberation, one who attains the sarupya-sayujya kind of liberation reaches Vaikunth. But Jivanji rejected all four kinds of liberation. One who attains liberation there is granted four arms just like God's own — but by becoming like God, by becoming non-dual (advait) with him, one does not obtain prem-bhakti (loving devotion). Moreover, God does not dwell in a Vaikunth devoid of loving devotion. It is said in the Pancharatra:

_Naaham vasami vaikunthe yoginam hridaye na cha, madbhakta yatra gayanti tatra tishthami Narada_ (O Narada! I do not dwell in Vaikunth, nor even in the hearts of yogis — but wherever my devotees sing devotional songs, there I dwell.)

_Na Hari vaikunthama, na Vrindavandham, jahan santki mandali, uhan milat hai Ram_ (Lord Ram does not dwell in Vaikunth, nor even in Vrindavan-dham — but wherever the devotional gathering of saints takes place, there Ram is met.)

_Na Hari vaikunthme, jogi hirde nahi, gyaani harijan hari tahan, dooja thor nahi._ ||19|| (Gyaniji Maharaj says: God does not dwell in Vaikunth, nor in the hearts of yogis — but wherever there is a devotee of Hari, there Hari dwells; nowhere else.)

_Satjug treta Jivana, vaikunth hamaro vaas, dwapar Gokul vasu, kaljug jahan nijdas._ ||41|| (Jivandasji Maharaj says God declares: In Satyug and Treta my dwelling was in Vaikunth, and in Dwapar I resided in Gokul, but in Kaliyug I dwell wherever my innermost devotees are.)

Raga Asavari:

_Narad santan jivan mero, man karam vachan bhajai je moko, to bohor na aave fero. (tek)
Vaikunthme vaaso nahi mero, Dwaravati na hoi,
jahan mero sant gaave, tahan mai nachu, santanko mukh joi._ ||1||
_Maira sant bhukha to mai bhukha, sant jamai mai jeemu,
jahan mero sant sauve, tahan mai jaagu, santan mahe ramu._ ||2||
_Sakal tirath santke charane charane, Lakshmi tanki dasi,
kaam krodh lobh moh maya, e charau karat khavasi._ ||3||
_Kahet Kabir suno bhai santo, e Harike mukhki vani,
Narad pratye santko mahima, te gaayo Sarangvani._ ||4||

(God told Narada: O Narada, the saints are my very life; those who worship me in mind, word, and deed will not come back again into the round of birth and death. [Refrain] I do not dwell in Vaikunth, nor in Dwarka; but wherever my saint sings, there I dance, gazing at the saint's face. [1] If my saint goes hungry, I too go hungry; if the saint eats, I eat; where my saint sleeps, there I stay awake, and I play within the saint. [2] All places of pilgrimage rest at the feet of my saints, and Lakshmi herself is their maidservant; desire, anger, greed, attachment, and delusion — all four serve them as attendants. [3] Kabir says, listen, O saints — this is the very word spoken by God's own mouth, the greatness of the saint that God sang to Narada in the raga Sarang in the Pancharatra. [4])

Das Kabirji explains: God said to Narada, "O Narada, the saints are dearer to me than my own life. Those who worship me with mind, speech, and action do not return again into the cycle of birth and death. I do not dwell in Vaikunth, nor in Dwarka — but wherever my saint sings devotional songs, I dance there, watching his face, delighting in him. If my saint is hungry, I too am hungry; when the saint eats, I eat. Where my saint sleeps, I stay awake, and I sport within the saint. All the places of pilgrimage rest at my saint's feet, and Lakshmiji is the saint's maidservant; desire, anger, greed, attachment, and delusion — all four serve him diligently." Kabirji says: listen, O saints — this is the very speech spoken directly from God's own mouth, which God spoke to Narada in the Pancharatra while describing the saint's glory.

Raga Ramgri:

_Maru Vrindavan chhe rudu re, Vaikunth nahi aavu,
nahi aavu Nandjina Lal, nahi aavu. (tek)
Besine rehvu ne tagtag jovu, nahi khavu nahi pivu re - Vaikunth nahi._ ||1||
_Vaiman moklo to moklo vehlu, hun aavish sauna pahelu re - Vaikunth nahi._ ||2||
_Brahmana lokto chhe ati kuda, vaasi Vrajna ruda re - Vaikunth nahi._ ||3||
_Je Vije be poliya hata, tene tatkshan melya kahadi re - Vaikunth nahi._ ||4||
_Narsaiyacho swami antarjami, tame sambhalne Sarangpani re - Vaikunth nahi._ ||5||

(My Vrindavan is lovely — I will not come to Vaikunth, I will not come, O beloved son of Nand, I will not come. [Refrain] There one must only sit and stare fixedly, with nothing to eat and nothing to drink — I will not come to Vaikunth. [1] If you send a heavenly chariot for me, send it quickly — I shall be the very first to come — I will not come to Vaikunth. [2] The worlds of Brahma are utterly false and hollow; the dwellers of Vraj are the true and lovely ones — I will not come to Vaikunth. [3] The two doorkeepers who stood there [Jay and Vijay] were at once thrown out — I will not come to Vaikunth. [4] O Lord of Narsaiyo, knower of all hearts — hear this, O Sarangpani [Krishna] — I will not come to Vaikunth. [5])

Once the cowherd boys insistently urged Lord Krishna, saying, "O Kanuda, you are our special friend — won't you show us your Vaikunth-dham? People praise Vaikunth so highly that we too have grown eager to see such a fine abode." Shri Krishna replied, "Oh, there's nothing there worth seeing, nothing enjoyable." But the cowherd boys, having grown tempted by hearing everyone extol Vaikunth, said, "Come now, friend! Being our special friend and yet hiding your own abode from us — that isn't right." There, he appeared four-armed, in his Chaturbhuj form, utterly inactive, engaged in no activity whatsoever, and without a trace of joy or exuberance. Seeing this dry, joyless atmosphere, the cowherd boys said, "Hey Krishna, where is Radha here? Where is the curd, where is the butter?" Then the Lord said, "Here dwell those who have attained moksha and been granted liberation, so there is no milk, curd, or butter here — those are found only in the land of Vraj." Seeing such a bland place, the disheartened cowherd boys, disappointed, said they did not care for this Vaikunth at all — they found Vrindavan far dearer. Narsinh Mehta composed a pada about this in the raga Ramgri (given above).

The cowherd boys say to Lord Krishna: "O beloved Krishna of Nandji, our own Vrindavan feels far dearer to us, so I shall not come to Vaikunth — for there, one must simply sit doing nothing at all, staring fixedly, with nothing whatsoever to eat or drink. So if you send a heavenly chariot to fetch us, send it quickly, so that I may be the very first to board it and come to your Vraj-dham. The people of this universe are exceedingly deceitful, while the residents of Vraj are truly excellent and lovely. From Vaikunth, two gatekeepers named Jay and Vijay were once thrown out. Narsinh Mehta's Lord Vishnu knows the innermost heart, so please accept my wish to come to Vraj."

_Vrindavan aur Vaikunthku, tolyo Tulsidas, bhari so nicho raha, halko gayo aakash_ (Tulsidas weighed Vrindavan and Vaikunth on a scale: the heavier one stayed low, and the lighter one rose up into the sky.)

Tulsidasji says: when devotees of God weighed Vrindavan and Vaikunth, the one that was heavier — Vrindavan — remained down here on earth, while Vaikunth, being the lighter one, had its pan rise up high into the sky.

_Karm chhape Vaikunth manhe, sarge bhelabhel, satjug sab gaye Jivana, kaljug lebe mail._ ||63|| (Ritual karma lies hidden within Vaikunth, and in heaven it is mingled everywhere; all of it departed in Satyug, but Kaliyug takes on its taint.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: devotees banished ritual observance (karmakand) into exile, and that karma hid itself away within Vaikunth, while in the heavenly realms karma became mixed into everything; and looking at Satyug, Dwapar, and all the other ages, it crept into japa, tapa, pilgrimage, vows, mantra recitation, spiritual practice, sacrifice, and the like. But in Kaliyug, devotees who practise single-minded devotion have driven it out entirely, banishing it into exile and casting it aside.

_Vaikunth laago rovane, sarag rahyo sir koot, taak sevak Jivana, ham beechme leene loot._ ||64|| (Vaikunth took to weeping, and heaven remained beating its head; look, O servant Jivan — we have plundered them right in the middle.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: Vaikunth was the abode for devotees of the heavenly realms who practised devotion through ritual and religious observance; devotees like us, who practise single-minded devotion, forcibly turned them back midway through true teaching. Thus we plundered, midway, the devotees of Vaikunth and the heavenly realms — and so poor Vaikunth began to grieve, and — as the passage itself repeats — we plundered the devotees of the heavenly realms midway, and so poor Vaikunth began to grieve, while the heavenly realms, despite making the most desperate efforts, striking their heads in anguish, grew utterly despondent and fell into deep sorrow.

_Kaha karau vaikunth hi jaay? Jahan nahi Nand, jahan na Jashoda, nahi jahan Gopi-Gwal, na gaay. Jahan nahi jal Jamunako nirmal, aur nahi kadamnaki thaant. Parmanand Prabhu chatur gwalini, Vraj-raj taji meri jaay balaay_ (What use is it even to go to Vaikunth? There is no Nand there, no Jashoda, no gopis or cowherds, not even cows; there is no pure water of the Yamuna, and no shade of the kadamba trees. Says Parmanand: the clever gopi declares — may my ill fate go wherever it will, rather than that I forsake the dust of Vraj.)

(Vraj is dear to me — I will not come to Vaikunth. Where would I find Nandji's son there? There is no graceful, thrice-bent Girdhari there, with beloved Radha resting at his side — beholding them is what cools my eyes. The clever gopi says: "Oh, what would I do by going to Vaikunth? What benefit is there in going to Vaikunth? For there is no Nandji there, nor Jashodaji, no gopis, no cowherds, not even cows; moreover there is no pure water of the Yamuna, nor the shade of the kadamba tree." Thus says Parmanand: the clever gopi declares that if any ill fate must befall her for forsaking Vraj, let it go elsewhere — if misfortune must come to her, she would rather it choose some other place.

_Sukh seja shital mahel, samukh sahaj bataai, kahai Kabir Vaikunthki, aas karai balaai._ ||21|| (A comfortable bed, a cool palace, and other such delights lie readily displayed before us — says Kabir, only one whose fate is to come to ruin would still long to attain Vaikunth.)

Das Kabirji says: leaving behind such an abode where comforts like a pleasing bed and a cooling palace are shown to us readily and effortlessly, only one destined for misfortune would still hope to attain that Vaikunth.

_Sarag narak nahi vanchhahi, aur Vaikunth Kailas, Chaturbhujdas darshan Ramka, paavai tabahi das._ ||11|| (Only when a devotee desires neither heaven nor hell, nor even Vaikunth or Kailas, does that servant — says Chaturbhujdas — attain the vision of Ram.)

Chaturbhujdas says: whoever harbours no desire to attain heaven or the splendour of hell, and also has no wish to obtain Vaikunth or Kailas, only such a devotee then attains the vision (darshan) of Ram.

_Narayanaparah sarve na kutashchana bibhyati, swargapavarganakeshvapi tulyarthadarshinah_ (Those devoted wholly to Narayan fear nothing whatsoever; they regard heaven, liberation, and hell alike, seeing them as equal in worth.) _Narayanparayan nihsang bhakt hai, vahan na narakse darta hai, na swargki iccha karta hai, aur na moksh hi chahta hai_ (A devotee devoted single-heartedly to Narayan, unattached to anything, neither fears hell, nor desires heaven, nor even longs for liberation.)

In the chapter on the grace bestowed upon Naranadas, the Samagam writes about Vaikunth: the Gokul-lila was established in the Dwapar age. In the Satyug and Treta ages, the Lord of Grace (Kripanath) resided in Vaikunth; in this Dwapar age he came to Shri Gokul, locking up Vaikunth behind him as he left. For this reason, the charming flute-player Lord is the true one; even Vaikunth could not prove itself supremely accomplished — that is, it could not establish God's rightful, true nature as its own possessor.

Adhyaru Maharaj writes, in the Prithvi Dhol, verse 8:

_Var chalyo Vaikunth ufaro, te pad siyal agamya e._ ||12|| _Pohoto var param pad mandir aapane, jaha rajaji Hari Parabrahm e._ ||13|| (The bridegroom set off, turning away from Vaikunth, toward that peaceful, unattainable state; he arrived at his own supreme abode, where Rajaji Hari, the Supreme Brahman, resides.)

The wedded Husband, the Supreme Brahman, set out toward his own abode — his own primeval Vrindavan-dham, situated above Vaikunth, supreme above all, beyond even the realms of Janalok and Tamalok. Understanding the greatness of that abode is exceedingly difficult for anyone. This Husband, the Supreme Brahman, arrived at his own most excellent mansion, the abode of which he himself, Lord Parabrahm, is the very master.

Sadguru Jivandasji Maharaj, in the couplets (sakhis) of the 21 Angas, as well as in the sakhis on the union of Name and Form, has presented Vaikunth in many different ways.

_Tan man arpe Ramku, to de Vaikunthko dham, guru charane arpe Jivana, to charan kamal vishram._ ||31|| (Offer body and mind to Ram, and he grants the abode of Vaikunth; but offer them, O Jivan, at the Guru's feet, and he grants rest at his own lotus feet.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: if you surrender everything to God, he grants you a dwelling in the abode of Vaikunth. But if you accept surrender at the Guru's feet, he grants you the bliss of dwelling in God's own abode and serving him there.

_Mel mugat bhai Jivana, jab sadguru diyo updesh, sarag narak Vaikunthlu, jyu haar upaade kesh._ ||82|| (Liberation from all bondage came, O Jivan, when the Sadguru gave his teaching — heaven, hell, and Vaikunth were plucked away like hair pulled out in a fit of anger.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: when the Sadguru made clear the truth about Ram and Kabir, and gave the realization of the oneness between the two imperishable syllables (aksharas), then, as if in anger, like hair torn out from the head, the web of illusion woven of heaven, hell, and the rest was cast off and flung away.

_Swarg nagar dono taje, nahi Vaikunthki aas, Ramnaam bhaj Jivana, jahan sadguru shabd vishwas._ ||108|| (Forsake both the city of heaven and hope of Vaikunth — chant Ram's name, O Jivan, and place your faith in the Sadguru's word.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: if you are to walk only by placing faith in the Sadguru's teaching, then hold that faith and trust, abandon all thoughts of the higher or lower realms, whether heaven or hell, and, without any desire to attain even Vaikunth, simply chant the name of Ram.

_Ham jaanyo Hari dhunkdo, Vaikunth peli paar, vebhi nedo Jivana, jo sadguru hoy kripal._ ||143|| (We had thought Hari to be far off, beyond Vaikunth on the other shore; but he is nearer still, O Jivan, if the Sadguru turns gracious.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: we used to think that God dwelt very far away, on the distant far shore of Vaikunth, separate from this earthly world. But if the Sadguru's grace descends, he is found even nearer than that, right here in this very world.

_Sant darshanku Jivana, aash kare Vaikunth, Vaikunth bapareki kaha chali, jo vanchhe Kamlakanth._ ||7|| (Even Vaikunth longs, O Jivan, for the sight of a saint — what power has poor Vaikunth, when even the Lord of Lakshmi himself yearns for it?)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: even Vaikunth keeps longing for the sight of a saint. Alas, what power does poor Vaikunth have — even the Lord of Vaikunth, Lakshmi's own husband, keeps longing for it too.

_Nirvasik je Jivana, Harijan taaka naam, sarag narak Vaikunth taj, te samre Sitaram._ ||16|| (Whoever is free of all desire, O Jivan, that alone is the true name of a devotee of Hari — forsaking desire for heaven, hell, or Vaikunth, he keeps remembering Sitaram.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: whoever is free of all worldly cravings, that alone is worthy of the name "devotee of Hari" (harijan); he forsakes the cravings for heaven, hell, and Vaikunth, and continually keeps remembering Sitaram.

_Kotik Vaikunth upre, Shri Vrindavan sukh dham, taathe neeki Jivana, sant sangat vishram._ ||30|| (Above tens of millions of Vaikunths stands Shri Vrindavan, the abode of joy — but better still, O Jivan, is rest found in the company of saints.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: more than crores of Vaikunths, Shri Vrindavan is the abode that gives God greater joy; and greater joy still than that lies in taking rest in the company of saints.

_Aag jalo Vaikunthma, jahan sant samagam nahi, taathe neeki Jivana, Shri Bansivatki chhanhi._ ||31|| (Let Vaikunth burn in fire, where the company of saints cannot be found — better, O Jivan, is the shade of the sacred Bansivat.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: let Vaikunth burn and be destroyed by fire, if the company of saints cannot be found there; better than that is to dwell in the shade of the Bansivat tree.

_Aag jalo Vaikunthme, jahan sant samagam nahi, bhagat viyoge dukhiyo bhayo, uhan jan to aave nahi._ ||32|| (Let Vaikunth burn, where the company of saints cannot be found — the Lord grew sorrowful there for want of his devotees, for no devotee ever comes there.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: let that Vaikunth, where the company of saints cannot be found, burn and be destroyed by fire — for there, God grew sorrowful from separation from his devotees, because devotees of Hari never go there.

_Mai Gokulma vaas vasu, kabhu Shesh sukhasan dham, kabhu ek Vaikunth Jivana, kabhu nagar Ayodhya dham._ ||36|| (I make my true dwelling in Gokul; yet at times I dwell in the blissful abode upon Shesh's couch, sometimes, O Jivan, in Vaikunth, and sometimes in the town of Ayodhya.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: God declares, "I dwell permanently in Gokul; but in another form, at times I stay in the blissful abode of the Kshirsagar, upon Sheshnag's couch, and at times in Vaikunth, and at times in the town of Ayodhya."

_Sir Sanakadik Jivana, chhoda Vaikunth manhi, sant sangat sapne nahi, to parampad kaise paay._ ||65|| (Even the great Sanakadik, O Jivan, were left behind within Vaikunth — never even in dream did they keep the company of saints, so how then could they attain the supreme state?)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: misfortune befell even the Sanakadik sages, being left within Vaikunth, because they had never, even in a dream, kept the company of saints — so how, then, could they ever attain the supreme state?

_Aadha mata kaun kaamka, jo paave Vaikunthko dham, taathe jagat bhali Jivana, kabahu sant sangat vishram._ ||73|| (What use is a half-finished creed that only wins one the abode of Vaikunth? Better, O Jivan, is this world, where one may sometimes find rest in the company of saints.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: what use is such a half-hearted, incomplete devotion to God — devoid of service to saints — that only wins, by its merit, the mere attainment of Vaikunth-dham? Better than that is reckoned this worldly life, for in it one can at least sometimes find the chance to rest in the company of saints.

_Mukh maru ta daasko, ninda kare jo koy, Vaikunththi daarahu, Jivan yu barad mohe._ ||136|| (Whoever speaks ill of that servant, I shall strike him on the mouth — this is my vow, O Jivan, even should I have to reach into Vaikunth to do it.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: God declares, "Whether they are devotees of Shiv, Brahma, or the other gods, like Ravan and his kind — if they speak ill of devotion to me or of my devotees, or grow jealous of them, then, without fear or shame of them, I will speak to them plainly, straight to their face. And wherever they may be — Vaikunth, Shivlok, Brahmalok, or anywhere else — if they speak such ill words, I will threaten them and make them stop speaking. That is my vow; that is my rule."

_Ved katebthi Jivana, nyare Harike das, swarg narak Vaikunth taj, kare Hari charanki aash._ ||154|| (Free from the Vedas and the Book, O Jivan, are Hari's true devotees — forsaking heaven, hell, and Vaikunth, they hold hope only in Hari's feet.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: God's exclusive devotees remain indifferent to the ritual observances prescribed by the Vedas, Puranas, or the Quran. Renouncing heaven and the rest, they hold their hope in taking refuge only at God's lotus feet.

_Vaikunth chhanhi Jivana, nyare Harike das, sol-kalasu shaamlo, sakal sevak sukh dham._ ||33|| (Leaving Vaikunth behind, O Jivan, Hari's true devotee is set apart — the dark Lord, full of sixteen powers, becomes the abode of joy for all his servants.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: God set his intent on leaving Vaikunth behind and dwelling in the village of Gokul instead. That Lord Krishna is endowed with sixteen kalas (perfections). Gokul is that pure, blissful village which gives joy to all devotees; there he resolved to dwell.

_Pahela dash avatar hai, dooja Vaikunth jaan, treejo Omkar Jivana, chautha ghatghat maan._ ||5|| (First are the ten avatars; know the second to be Vaikunth; the third, O Jivan, is Omkar; and the fourth is the one dwelling in every heart.)

Jivandasji Maharaj, listing the seven honest-looking thieves, says: first, the ten avatars are the honest thief; know the second to be Vaikunth; the third is Omkar; and the fourth thief is the one who calls the divine dwelling in every heart the complete Parabrahm — that too, believe my word, is an honest-looking thief.

_Sar Sanakadik Jivana, chhodo Vaikunth manhe, Sitapati bhootal vase, sant samagam manhe._ ||22|| (The great Sanakadik, O Jivan, were left resting within Vaikunth — but Sitapati [Ram] dwells here on earth, wherever the company of saints takes place.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: great sages like Sanakadik were left behind to rest within the abode of Vaikunth, left there still seeking God — but Sitapati Ram dwells here on this earth, wherever the gathering of saints takes place.

_Darshan karan doheli, biraha Vaikunth manhi, ko ek Harijan mile Jivana, ham baithe taaki chhanhi._ ||9|| (In Vaikunth, [God] suffers the anguish of separation, for it is hard to find a sight of loving devotees there — should even a single devotee of Hari be found, O Jivan, there I sit in his shade.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: loving saints and devotees do not go to Vaikunth, so it is hard to obtain their darshan there; God, growing restless with the pain of that separation, seeks the sight of his loving devotees, and should even one devotee-saint be found on earth, I dwell in his company.

_Mai Vaikunthvasi Jivana, bohot rahyo udaas, Vrindavanki kunjma, Radhe sang vilas._ ||298|| (I, as a dweller of Vaikunth, O Jivan, remained deeply sorrowful — but in the groves of Vrindavan, in play with Radha, joy was found.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: God declares, "When I dwelt in Vaikunth, even though I had one such as Lakshmi to serve at my feet, my heart remained sorrowful. But when I sported with Radha in the groves of Vrindavan, I became joyful — I found the essence of love through Radha's company."

_Mai Vaikunthvasi Jivana, sab santanke viyog, Vrindavan sada rahu, bhav bhagat ras bhog._ ||299|| (I, dwelling in Vaikunth, O Jivan, suffered separation from all the saints; now I dwell forever in Vrindavan, enjoying the essence of loving, devoted worship.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: God declares, "I used to dwell in Vaikunth, but there I bore the sorrow of separation from all saints. So now I dwell always in Vrindavan, where I find the good fortune of relishing the essence of loving devotion and its tender delight."

_Kabir sant darshan van doheli, brahoni Vaikunth manhi, Ram Kabira jo mile, ham varte taaki chhanhi._ ||300|| (Kabir says: without the sight of a saint, that delight is hard to attain — its playing-ground lies within Vaikunth's expanse; but wherever Ram and the devotee-saint Kabir can be found together, there we abide, sheltered in that shade.)

Das Kabirji says: without the sight of a saint, the enjoyment of the tender delight of loving devotion is hard to attain. Its play-ground lies within Vaikunth, but if Lord Ram and the devotee-saint Kabir can be found together somewhere, we would rather remain, submissive, under their shelter.

_Kabir Ram bulava bhejiya, Kabire dino roy, jo sukh hai sant hil mil, so Vaikunth na hoy._ ||301|| (Kabir wept when Ram sent his summons — for the joy found in the fellowship of saints, mingled together, is not to be found in Vaikunth.)

Das Kabirji says: when the summons of God comes to one who has been in the company of saints, it brings deep sorrow — because the joy of intimate fellowship, gathering, and devotional worship found together with saints in satsang is not to be found in Vaikunth.

_Kabir mera man pankhi bhaya, ud gaya aakash, Vaikunth to khaali bhaya, Saheb santo paas._ ||305|| (Kabir: my mind became a bird and flew up into the sky; but Vaikunth was found empty — the Lord dwells near his saints.)

Das Kabirji says: in search of God, my mind flew up into the sky, like a bird, to Vaikunth — but Vaikunth lay empty of God; God dwells only near his saints.

_Sapt puripe Jivana, Vaikunthpe ati saar, Vrindavan sohamnu, jahan Radhe sang vihar._ ||306|| (Above the seven sacred cities, and above Vaikunth too, O Jivan, stands supreme the lovely Vrindavan, where God sports together with Radha.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: far more excellent than the seven sacred cities, and even more excellent than Vaikunth, is the surpassing, beautiful Vrindavan, where God sports together with Radha.

_Vaikunth chhodi Jivana, aayo Gokul manhi, Vrajsukh to tahan sapne nahi, mope rahyo na jaay._ ||311|| (Leaving Vaikunth, O Jivan, I came to Gokul — for even in dream, no joy like that of Vraj is found there, and so I could not remain.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: God declares, "I left Vaikunth and came into Gokul, because there the joy of Vraj is not found even in dream, and so I could not bear to stay there."

_Kabir nishkami nirmal dasha, pakde chaare khoote, kahe Kabir ta daaski, aash kare Vaikunth._ ||316|| (One free of all desire, dwelling in a pure state, holding firm on all four sides — says Kabir, even Vaikunth longs for such a devotee to come to it.)

Das Kabirji says: whoever is free of all desire, dwells in a state of pure devotion, and remains steadfast and unmoved on every side — even Vaikunth longs and hopes that such a devotee might one day come to it.

_Prahlad bichara kaha kare, kamanki dhundi naah, naame baaho Jivana, chhodo Vaikunth manh._ ||366|| (Poor Prahlad — what could he do, having found no bow of grace? Clinging only to the Name, O Jivan, he was sent away from Vaikunth.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: poor Prahlad was helpless — what could he do? He held no ill will at all toward God's Name or toward a Guru, in seeking the devotion of Name-and-Form through a Sadguru. But it was not possible for him to find one, so he clung only to God's Name — and for that, God sent him to his own abode.

Ghat-Ghatna (The One Dwelling in Every Heart) — In the Samagam, in the chapter on the Brahman of the world (maya), the second sakhi of the Garbhavali Anga is given, where it says: the thief who dwells in every heart means committing wrongful acts while believing oneself to possess the knowledge of Brahman.

_Mansa Devi ushni, taathe bhayo Omkar, ghatghat vyapak Jivana, so khole Nandadwar._ ||2|| (The Goddess Mansa arose, and from her came Omkar; that which pervades every heart, O Jivan, is the one who opens the door of Nand's house.)

Jivandasji Maharaj, in the Anga called Garbhavali (the wheel of the 84 lakh species of birth, in which the soul wanders entangled), says: at the beginning of creation, the illusory goddess named Mansa arose, and from her the Omkar-imbued (three-gunas) creation came forth. That very Supreme Being, whose essence pervades every single body in the world — that same Supreme Being sports in the courtyard of Nandji.

_Brahmagyani anusare, ghatghat vyapak Ram, hamare yu vrat Jivana, je Sitapatiko naam._ ||5|| (Those who know Brahman follow the Ram who pervades every heart — but our vow, O Jivan, is this: devotion only to the Name of Sitapati.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: those learned in the knowledge of Brahman, aspiring to know Brahman, worship with a spiritual sentiment the Ram who pervades every single limb of every heart. But our own rule is this: to worship only that name which is Sitapati Ram's name.

_Ghatghatma Hari lekhve, aape ho rahyo Brahm, meede hato Jivana, te shir par leeno karm._ ||15|| (Reckoning that Hari pervades every heart, one takes oneself to be Brahman — but O Jivan, one who was already effaced thereby draws that bondage of karma upon his own head.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: convinced that God pervades everyone and everything, a person sets out to become Brahman himself. But by doing so, he brings upon his own head a bondage of karma that had, in truth, no real existence at all.

_Jyu jalme pratibimb hai, tyu ghatghat vyapak Ram, guru prasade Jivana, paaiye mool Chandrako dhaam._ ||16|| (As a reflection falls in water, so does Ram, pervading every heart; by the Guru's grace, O Jivan, may we attain the true moon itself, not merely its reflection.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: just as the reflection of an object falls in water, so too does the reflected image of Lord Ram fall within every single heart. But through the Guru's grace, instead of settling for that reflection, we shall attain the true moon itself — Lord Ram, the real, original moon.

_Sanya seti Jivana, kabahu na kije rosh, aape ghatghat le rahyo, aape banayo dhosh._ ||17|| (Never grow angry with the Lord, O Jivan, nor resentful — he himself dwells within every heart by his own will, and he himself has set this whole universe running.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: never grow angry with God, never bring resentment or ill will against him, nor sulk against him — for God himself, of his own accord, is dwelling within every heart, and he himself has set this entire universe in motion.

_Ghatghat to Hari lekhve, pan sanya santo paas, dhua dharhar Jivana, taame kaiso baas._ ||19|| (We may reckon that Hari pervades every heart, but the Lord who is near his saints is different — like grasping at billowing smoke, O Jivan, what true dwelling could there be in that?)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: we understand that God pervades every heart — but that is Maryada Purushottam (the Lord bound by cosmic limits), whereas the God who is near his saints is Purna Purushottam, the complete, unbounded Lord. Just as one might try to grasp handfuls of billowing smoke, yet the supreme essence could never truly dwell within that smoke, so too is it futile to strive to grasp the God-in-every-heart as though grasping at smoke.

_Ko kahe Hari soon aakashme, ko kahe Hari ghatghat manhi, sadguru bataayo Jivana, Shri Bansivatki chhanhi._ ||78|| (Some say Hari dwells in the empty sky, some say Hari dwells within every heart; but the Sadguru showed, O Jivan, the shade of the sacred Bansivat.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: among those of differing opinions, some say that God resides in the empty void of the sky, while others say God resides everywhere, within every single body — but the Sadguru showed that God, in his true form, resides at the sacred Bansivat.

_Ghatghat vyapak Jivana, pan Antaryami ek, mai balihari ta daaski, jahan sadguru shabd vivek._ ||120|| (God pervades every heart, O Jivan — yet the indwelling Witness is one alone; I offer myself in devotion to that servant, wherever the Sadguru's word brings true discernment.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: the indwelling God, the Antaryami, pervades every single body everywhere. Yet that divine essence is but one alone; blessed, therefore, are those devotees who worship while placing their faith in the Sadguru's teaching — God himself declares, "I sacrifice myself for such devotees."

_Sadguru samjhaayo Jivana, gupt pragat je baat, ek roop ghatghat vase, ek Sitapati Raghunath._ ||121|| (The Sadguru explained, O Jivan, the truth both hidden and manifest — one form dwells within every heart, yet the one true Lord is Sitapati Raghunath.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says that the God-essence (bhagavat-tattva) is secretly manifest in every body (ghat). The true guru has revealed its mystery — that this one form of God exists in the form of Ramchandra, the lord of Sita (Sitapati).

_ghatghat vyapak jivana | sitapatiko roop ||
guru krupa ta daasku | ja ghat naam swaroop ||122||_ (Pervading every body, O Jivana, is the form of Sitapati [Ram]. By the guru's grace, that devotee attains the Name-form present within every body.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: the radiance of this God, Sitapati Ram's form, pervades every body. But it is in the body of that devotee upon whom the guru's grace rests that God dwells in the form of the Name.

_hast mastak aave nahi | ghatghat vyapak ram ||
sadguru samjhayo jivana | je samro sitaram ||140||_ (Ram, who pervades every body, cannot be grasped by hand or by the intellect. The true guru has explained, O Jivana: remember and recite that Sitaram.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: that God who pervades the body of everyone cannot be brought under anyone's control or grasp, nor caught within anyone's intellect. Remember and worship that same Lord Sitaram — this is what the true guru has explained.

_ghatghat vyapak ek | pan preet van pachho osare ||
mukh chave vaans | ikh kaaj tene sare ||92||_ (The One pervades every body alike, but without love it withdraws again — as the mouth chews on bare reed, which does not serve the purpose that sugarcane does.)

_anant kot vasidato | sakal pankhka mool ||
narsandh ghatghat pekhiye | gaya te sanse sool ||148||_ (the fine turns of this couplet are not fully clear [unclear]; its general sense continues the theme that the one root of all is seen present in every body, and doubt's thorn departs for those who see this)

_nij mool nij naam hai | daasi palowe paay ||
so ghatghat vyapak jivana | brij kul taare gaay ||84||_ (His own root is His own Name; the handmaiden [Lakshmiji] massages His feet in service. That very one, O Jivana, who pervades every body, tends the cows in the Brij clan.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: the God-essence has its own principal seat in His Name. Lakshmiji herself serves at the feet of that God who bears the divine Name; devotees of the dasya-bhava (the disposition of a handmaiden), full of loving devotion, worship Him in that same spirit. Such a God-essence pervades every body, in all that moves and does not move. That God grazes the cows in the pastures of Vraj-mandal.

Adhyaruji Maharaj says in the Harsh Bhavan (chapter):

_jotam janjan joojvo | ane jag sacharachar soy ||
ravi aapope mandine | patra vilane joy ||34||_ (Looking closely, God appears different from person to person, and in this moving and unmoving world too He is that same one appearing in different forms — like the one sun, seen reflected differently when placed before different vessels.)

God appears different to each and every person. And in this world, in all that moves and does not move, He, the very same One, dwells in different forms. Just as when we look at one and the same sun, it appears different in different vessels [of water], so too the Lord, the very same One, dwells in different bodies.

In the Brahmanda Purana, Ram said to Vasishtha:

_yatha anek kumbheshu ravir eko api drushyate |
tatha sarveshu bhooteshu chintaniyo asau sada ||_ (Just as, though there are many pots, the reflection of the one sun appears different in each, so too in all beings the one Supreme Soul appears as though different — this should always be reflected upon.)

Just as, though there are many pots, the reflection of the one sun appears different in each, so too in all bodies, the one and same Supreme Soul appears as though different. This should always be reflected upon.

_udakpatra sahastreshu jyotir eko avabhasate |
tathaik aatma sarvatra vastuto bhaasate vibhuh ||_ (Just as there may be thousands of pots filled with water, but the light of the moon or sun falls equally and alike in all of them, so too the Supreme Soul remains ever radiant, alike, in all beings and things.)

Just as there may be thousands of pots filled with water, but the light of the moon or the sun falls equally the same in all of them, in that same way, the Supreme Soul too remains ever radiant in all living beings and in all things.

An illustration: once, at some place, people of all different sects and opinions were sitting together, arguing among themselves about their differing views. No one was ready to accept anyone else's position, and everyone kept praising his own view. In the end, the quarrel reached the point where sticks were about to be raised. At that point, one of the saints among them spoke up: "Brothers, why are you engaging in this useless argument? Look —"

_ghatghatme hari ek hai | taame nahi vishek ||
jaiso footi aarsi | khand khand mukh ek ||_ (Hari is one alone within every body — in that there is no difference. It is like a broken mirror: in each shard, the same one face is seen.)

Hearing this, everyone spoke as one voice:

_tileshu tailam dadhi niva sarpi | jaranya strotassu aranishu chaagnih |
evam aatma-aatmani sannigruhyate | satyena inam tapasa yo anupashyati ||_ (As oil is in sesame seed, ghee is in curd, water is in a mountain spring, and the flame of fire is in the arani [kindling-wood], so Parbrahma, the Supreme Soul, is present everywhere.)

As oil is in sesame seed, ghee is in curd, water is in a mountain spring, and the flame of fire is in the arani (fire-wood used for kindling), in that same way Parbrahma, the Supreme Soul, is present everywhere.

_sab ghat chhaya ramki | pragat ghat hai daas ||
aur ghatme gop hai | unme bhaya prakash ||_ (The reflection of Ram is in every body; but it is manifest openly in the body of His devotee. In other bodies it remains hidden, though its light is present within them.)

Gnaniji Maharaj says: in all bodies there is a reflection of God, but in the body of the saint (devotee), He is present in manifest form. In other bodies, He remains hidden/secret. Thus His influence pervades the entire world.

_gnani sab ghat antar ram hai | jyon jal madhye aakash |
nishchal jal e nirmala | haale taame naash ||65||_ (Ram is within every body, O wise one — like the sky reflected in water. In water that is still, this [reflection] is clear; when it stirs, it is lost.)

Gnaniji Maharaj says: Ram dwells within, inside every single body. He remains there just as the reflection of the sky remains within water. But in water that is not stirring, that reflection appears clear; and if it stirs, that reflection is lost.

_nishchal jal e daas hai | haale soi jiv ||
gnani gurugaam dekhiya | sadhu janme piv ||69||_ (The still water is the devotee; that which stirs is the jiva [the ordinary soul]. The wise one, having seen through the guru's teaching, knows the Beloved dwells among the saintly.)

Gnaniji Maharaj says: the water that is still/steady represents the saint-devotee, and the water that stirs represents the ordinary jivatma (individual soul). Through this mystery revealed by the guru, it is understood that God dwells within saint-devotees.

_sab ghat bhitar me basu | mohi milai na koy ||
jo kachhu karu so mai karu | naam bandeka hoy ||5||_ (I dwell within every body, yet none finds Me. Whatever I do, I alone do it, but it is the servant's name that is spoken as the doer.)

Das Kabirji says, in the Aap Alekh Anga (chapter): "I (God) dwell within every body, yet no one finds Me. Whatever I do, I alone do it, but the doer's name that gets spoken is that of the devoted servant."

_sab ghat bhitar me khara (ram hai) | esa aap sujaan |
aape aapso bandhiya | aape bhaya ajaan ||_ (Within every body dwells the True One [Ram] — know this for yourself with certainty. You yourself have bound yourself, and you yourself have become the ignorant one.)

Das Kabirji says: be certain, in this way, that God truly resides within every body. It is by your own mind that you become bound in bondage; it appears that you have fallen into bondage without having understood this mystery.

_mai manme jaana huta | aur na tha ko paas ||
to sab ghat bhitar ko lahu | sab ghat mero vaas ||8||_ (I knew, within my own mind, one hidden thing — that there was no one else beside Me. So then whom should I take to be within every body? For every body is my own dwelling.)

Das Kabirji says God speaks thus: "I knew, within my own mind, a hidden secret — that there was no one else beside Me. So then, whom should I take to be within all these bodies? For it is I Myself who dwell within every single body."

_mujsa sabko dekhiye | par muj sarikha nahi koy ||
muj jaisa manme rahai | nahi na dekho doy ||7||_ (Everyone will appear like Me, yet none is truly My equal; but if the same disposition as Mine dwells within one's mind, then nothing but Myself will be seen.)

Das Kabirji says: everyone will appear to be like Me, but there will be no one equal to Me; yet if the same disposition as Mine remains within one's mind, then no other besides Myself will be perceived.

_ish eko avagantavyo | naana mata nivishtakaih |
bhinne kache yatha murtir | bhidyate vastuto aprithak ||_ (This one Ishwar is to be known as present everywhere alike by people of every differing doctrine — just as in a broken mirror the reflected face appears in many separate pieces, though in truth it remains one.)

People holding different kinds of doctrines/opinions ought to know that this one Ishwar (God) is present everywhere as one alone — just as in a broken mirror the face appears in many separate pieces, yet in truth it is one.

_sab hi ghatme hari base | jyon girisutme jyoti |
gnan guru manme rahai | nahi na dekho doy ||7||_ (Hari dwells within every single body, as light dwells within the mountain's daughter [i.e., pervading it through and through]. When the guru's knowledge abides in the mind, nothing but that One is seen.)

Das Kabirji says: God dwells in every single body. Just as sparks of fire do not come out of a flint stone unless it is struck against iron, in that same way, without a guru who gives us understanding, the God present within us cannot be made manifest.

Aiming at those followers of the path of knowledge (jnana-marg) who, by recognizing the God present in every body as the Supreme Soul, wish to declare themselves as Brahma — it is true that, since Parmeshwar is present in every body, there is a principle by which one is a form of Brahma, but only as a fragment/portion of the Complete Brahma (Purna Brahma); yet these Brahma-jnanis (self-styled knowers of Brahma) force upon everyone the claim that they themselves are the Complete Brahma in full. Therefore Kabirji, in the Kaami Anga (chapter), has exposed and censured them.

_kabir gnani to nidhadak bhaya | mane nahi shank ||
indri kere bas pare | bhugate vishaye nihshank ||36||_ (Kabir says: these men of knowledge have become so bold that they hold no shame; fallen under the sway of the senses, they indulge in sensory pleasures without any hesitation.)

Das Kabirji says: these so-called men of knowledge have become so bold and shameless that they keep no shame of any kind — they have become subject to their senses, and without any doubt, fear, or hesitation, they indulge in sensory pleasures.

_kabir gnani mool gamaiya | aape bhaya kartar ||
tathe to sansari bhula | manme rahe darta ||37||_ (Kabir says: these men of knowledge have lost their very roots, having come to believe themselves the Doer. Compared to them, worldly people, mistaken as they are, at least remain fearful [and restrained] in their minds.)

Das Kabirji says: these men of knowledge have abandoned every trace of shame and propriety from the very root, and have come to believe as if they themselves have become the Doer, the "I am Brahma" Supreme Being. Compared to them, ordinary worldly people are better — for they, keeping worldly shame and propriety, live fearfully within the bounds of honor and restraint.

_kabir bhagati bigadi bhudeve | kathi kathi brahmagyan ||
gatrandaki sundari | kyon pave santan ||39||_ (Kabir says: the earth-gods [the Brahmins] have ruined devotion by preaching, again and again, the talk of Brahma-knowledge. How can the wife of an impotent man ever obtain a child?)

Das Kabirji says: those called "gods on earth" — the Brahmins — by preaching, again and again, the talk of Brahma-jnana (knowledge of Brahma), have ruined loving devotion (prem-bhakti). Just as the wife of an impotent man cannot obtain a child, in the same way, how can such feeble followers of Brahma-jnana ever attain true devotion?

(Raga Ashavari)

_santo sab hi ved kul mahi | tathe rogi jive nahi ||tek||
kahe harie gopi khandhe lidhi | aisi bhagati dradhave ||
jaisi sune taisi man upaje | tam lahar vikhki aave ||1||
gnan kathi gnan dradhave | trigun nadime bore ||
brahmagyaniku kahu thaur nahi | ya vidh bhagati na hoy re ||2||
puran brahma davanal pidho | giri govardhan dhari |
sol sahastra sang soi biraje | aap sada brahmachari ||3||
karma jaal katveke karan | sapanata thasab koi |
vedna jadi kachhu or | kupath padchya sab koi ||4||
sanskritme shukjie kahiya | prakrat santan vani |
lobh lahar aur vikhe vaasna | taame khenchatani ||5||
vis varaska purkha sunta | sol varaski naari |
kahat kabir bhali samjhai | bhulya chor katari ||6||_ (O saints, everyone is caught within the fold of the Vedas, and so the ill of [wrong] sentiment does not leave them; they say Hari once seated the gopi on his shoulder, pressing home such [a coarse notion of] devotion — whatever filth one hears, the mind conceives the same, and waves of poison arise. Talking knowledge upon knowledge, they drown all in the river of the three gunas; for the Brahma-jnani there is no true resting place — devotion cannot come by this way. The Complete Brahma who bore Mount Govardhan drank the forest-fire; that same one dwells amid sixteen thousand women, yet remains ever a Brahmachari. To cut the net of karma, everyone became entangled instead; being bound to the Vedas alone, everyone has fallen upon a wrong path. Shukji told it in Sanskrit, and the saints in the vernacular tongue — yet the waves of greed and poisonous desire keep pulling [such people] back and forth. Young men of twenty listen, and women of sixteen listen — says Kabir, though it was well explained, the deluded ones lost the very knife/key [of true understanding].)

Das Kabirji says: O saints! All the followers of the path of knowledge are trapped in the mass of the Vedas, and therefore, afflicted with this disease of [false] sentiment, they cannot hold their footing on the path of devotion. And these preachers of knowledge say that God once seated the gopi Radha upon His own shoulder — trying in this way to impress upon people this kind of obscene form of devotion — so that whatever filth is heard, the mind is tempted to do the same, and waves of sensual desire arise. These Brahma-jnanis, by repeatedly preaching this talk of knowledge — that Brahma alone dwells in all — impress upon people that they may indulge in sensory pleasures, and thereby drown everyone in the river of the three gunas' sensory pleasure. For such base, degraded so-called knowers of Brahma, there is no possibility whatsoever, anywhere in the world, of attaining supreme happiness. Because, believing that everything is of the nature of Brahma and behaving in this way in sensual desire, devotion to God cannot occur. If you call yourself "I am Brahma" and claim that you yourself are Brahma, then know that you will not be able to do what Shri Krishna, the Complete Brahma who held up Mount Govardhan, did — for he drank up the forest-fire. Such a capable, all-powerful Parbrahma, Shri Krishna, can remain seated amidst sixteen thousand women, entirely free of any disturbance [of passion]. In this way, even while dwelling among women, he remained ever the unbroken celibate (Brahmachari). To cut the net of karmic bondage, everyone used to listen to the character/deeds of Krishna, but true devotion was not obtained through the path of the Vedas, and instead everyone fell into a wrong, crooked path. Shukdev has described the divine play (leela) of Krishna in Sanskrit within the Bhagavat, and saints have sung the virtues of Krishna in the vernacular language — but because the waves of greed of self-interested people are directed towards sensory desire, they persist stubbornly in wishing to perform love-play like Krishna's. A young man of twenty years and a woman of sixteen years, hearing of such love-play, wrongly took it amiss — but just as, when a thief goes to commit a theft and forgets his main tool, the deed cannot be accomplished, in the same way, these so-called knowers of Brahma have missed the real, true mystery [of devotion], and therefore they will not attain a good end (sadgati).
